Algebra.title: Algebra
Algebra.description: Algebra studies structures defined by operations and the laws, morphisms, and symmetries that organize them.

fields.title: Associative rings and algebras
fields.description: Noncommutative rings and finite-dimensional associative algebras, including division and central simple algebras, quaternion algebras, polynomial identities, nil ideals and Hopf algebras. Group rings are under Group Theory.

fields.title: Lie algebras and nonassociative structures
fields.description: Lie algebras and their structure and representations, free Lie algebras, Poisson algebras, and racks and quandles.

fields.title: Algebraic identities and operations
fields.description: Polynomial and product identities, sum-of-squares identities, functional equations on rings, and elementary operations on functions and sets.

fields.title: Polynomials and power series
fields.description: Univariate and multivariate polynomials and formal power series as algebraic objects: coefficients, derivations, symmetric polynomials, irreducibility, polynomial maps and rational series.

fields.title: Zeros of polynomials
fields.description: Location, counting and multiplicity of the zeros of polynomials: real-rootedness, stability, interlacing, root bounds and Sturm sequences.

fields.title: Orthogonal polynomials and polynomial sequences
fields.description: Classical and combinatorial families of polynomials, their recurrences and generating functions, and orthogonality via Favard's theorem, J-fractions and Riordan arrays.

AlgebraicGeometry.title: Algebraic Geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.description: Algebraic geometry studies spaces cut out by polynomial equations and translates between their geometric and algebraic invariants.

fields.title: Schemes and morphisms
fields.description: The scheme-theoretic foundations of algebraic geometry: points, immersions, smooth morphisms, varieties over a field and properties that persist under base change.

fields.title: Varieties and projective geometry
fields.description: Classical algebraic geometry of affine and projective varieties: hypersurfaces and their singularities, tangent spaces, plane configurations, intersection multiplicities, linear systems and birational maps.

fields.title: Algebraic curves
fields.description: Algebraic curves and their invariants, including divisors, the genus, Jacobians and the Abel–Jacobi map.

fields.title: Elliptic curves
fields.description: Elliptic curves given by Weierstrass equations, their points over finite fields and number fields, torsion, reduction and Galois representations.

fields.title: Arithmetic geometry
fields.description: Rational points and point counts of varieties over number fields and finite fields, including the Mordell conjecture and the Weil conjectures.

Analysis.title: Analysis
Analysis.description: Analysis studies limits, approximation, continuity, and infinite-dimensional spaces of functions and operators.

fields.title: Real functions and calculus
fields.description: Functions of one or several real variables: differentiation, partial derivatives and multivariable calculus, the Riemann integral and evaluation of definite integrals, continuity and pathological functions, and functional equations on the reals.

subfields.title: Differential calculus of one variable
subfields.description: Derivatives of real functions of one real variable: mean-value and second-derivative tests, Taylor polynomials and remainders, Borel's lemma, interchange of limits and derivatives, monotone and C^n gluing results; not nowhere-differentiable constructions (see continuity subfield).

subfields.title: Multivariable calculus
subfields.description: Functions on R^n: partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, implicit functions, regular level sets and tangent spaces, curve length, Green's theorem, multivariable Taylor expansions and counterexamples about mixed partials or continuity at the origin.

subfields.title: Riemann integration and definite integrals
subfields.description: The Riemann integral via tagged partitions, iterated-integral formulas, moments, and closed-form evaluations of specific definite integrals (Serret's integral, integrals of 1/(1+u^n), areas between cosine powers, sinc squared); integrals defining a named special function go to Special functions.

subfields.title: Continuity, regularity and functional equations
subfields.description: Fine structure of real functions: Blumberg's theorem, continuous nowhere-differentiable functions (Weierstrass, Takagi), the rising sun lemma, approximate continuity, midpoint convexity, and the Cauchy, exponential and almost-additive functional equations including Hyers–Ulam stability.

fields.title: Inequalities
fields.description: Classical inequalities for sums, sequences, means and integrals of real or complex numbers: Hardy, Hilbert, Carleman, Wirtinger, Opial, Landau–Kolmogorov, Hermite–Hadamard, Kantorovich and Popoviciu, power-sum and elementary log/exp bounds; inequalities stated with Sobolev norms go to Function spaces, eigenvalue inequalities to Operator theory.

fields.title: Sequences, series and summability
fields.description: Convergence of numerical sequences and series and of series of functions, summability methods and Tauberian theorems, and closed-form evaluation of infinite series and products.

subfields.title: Convergence of sequences and series
subfields.description: Convergence tests (root test, rearrangement theorem, Stolz–Cesàro), normal and uniform convergence of series of functions, and specific limits of sequences and partial sums.

subfields.title: Summability and Tauberian theorems
subfields.description: Matrix summability methods (Silverman–Toeplitz, Cesàro means, permanent methods) and Tauberian theorems of Tauber, Hardy–Littlewood, Wiener and Newman.

subfields.title: Series for π, ζ(3) and other constants
subfields.description: Series and infinite products evaluating constants: π, Catalan's constant, Euler's constant, √2, ζ(3), reciprocal central binomial sums.

subfields.title: Trigonometric and harmonic-number series
subfields.description: Closed forms for series in powers of sin, cos or tan, central binomial series in trigonometric arguments, partial-fraction series of trigonometric functions, and identities with harmonic or odd harmonic numbers, as in Ramanujan's notebooks Chapter 9.

subfields.title: Power series and series transformations
subfields.description: Identities and transformations of power series and exponential-type series: Lagrange inversion and the tree function, Abel- and Jensen-type exponential series, coefficients of exp of a power series and Newton's identities for summable sequences, transformations of factorial series and Taylor-shift transformations, and Touchard / generalized Bell series.

fields.title: Asymptotic analysis
fields.description: Asymptotic expansions and methods: Euler–Maclaurin and Watson's lemma, Laplace-type integrals, coefficient asymptotics of power series (Bender's lemma), Stirling-type and inverse-factorial expansions, and asymptotic expansions of power sums, Lambert series and log sums; complex-analytic saddle-point results on entire functions go to Complex analysis.

fields.title: Special functions
fields.description: Named transcendental functions and their series, integral representations and identities: gamma and digamma, hypergeometric functions, exponential and logarithmic integrals, Lambert W, Bessel, Dickman, Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions, and elliptic functions (elliptic-function topics sit directly in the field).

subfields.title: Gamma and digamma functions
subfields.description: The gamma, digamma and trigamma functions: series and integral representations, factorial series, growth bounds against exponentials, and Ramanujan's digamma identities.

subfields.title: Hypergeometric functions
subfields.description: Generalized and basic hypergeometric series and their summation theorems (Gauss, Dougall, Dixon, Klamkin, Frisch). Orthogonal polynomial families go to Algebra/orthogonal-polynomials.

subfields.title: Exponential, logarithmic and related functions
subfields.description: Exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric-type functions and their relatives: exponential integral E1 and Ein, logarithmic integral, Lambert W, logistic function, x^y = y^x, exponential sums, Mittag-Leffler expansion of 1/(e^u − 1), modified Bessel functions, Dickman–de Bruijn function, Bell-polynomial functions.

subfields.title: Bernoulli polynomials, polylogarithms and Clausen functions
subfields.description: Bernoulli and Euler polynomials and their generating-function identities, Berndt's φ_r and power-difference series, Clausen functions, the inverse tangent integral and dilogarithm identities; results whose content is values of ζ, Dirichlet L or β functions belong to NumberTheory.

fields.title: Complex analysis
fields.description: Holomorphic and meromorphic functions of one and several complex variables: Cauchy theory, entire functions, conformal and univalent maps, zeros of polynomials, and Hilbert and Banach spaces of analytic functions.

subfields.title: Complex integration, residues and singularities
subfields.description: Contour integrals, Cauchy's theorem, residues, argument principle, Rouché, Laurent series, isolated singularities (Casorati–Weierstrass, great Picard), Schwarz reflection, Looman–Menchoff, normal families and local properties of holomorphic functions on discs and annuli.

subfields.title: Entire and meromorphic functions
subfields.description: Growth and value distribution of entire and meromorphic functions: Wiman–Valiron theory and maximum term, Hayman admissibility, Weierstrass factorization, Mittag-Leffler, Liouville-type rigidity, preimages and zeros/ones on lines.

subfields.title: Geometric function theory
subfields.description: Conformal and univalent maps: Riemann mapping, Koebe and Bloch theorems, Schwarz–Pick and half-plane self-maps, starlike and univalent coefficient problems, Loewner equation, holomorphic motions.

subfields.title: Polynomials in the complex plane
subfields.description: Analytic behaviour of complex polynomials: location of zeros (Eneström–Kakeya, Sendov's problem, Jentzsch), flat and Littlewood polynomials, complementary polynomials and sup norms on the unit circle. Algebraic properties of polynomials go to Algebra; Mahler measure goes to NumberTheory.

subfields.title: Several complex variables
subfields.description: Holomorphic functions on C^n: Hartogs extension and separate analyticity, Weierstrass preparation, complex Hessians.

subfields.title: Spaces of analytic functions
subfields.description: Hardy, Bergman, Dirichlet and Fock spaces and their reproducing kernels, H^∞, boundary behaviour (Fatou, F. and M. Riesz), cyclicity and polynomial density.

fields.title: Potential theory
fields.description: Harmonic and subharmonic functions in the plane and in R^n, harmonic conjugates, the Newton and logarithmic potentials and fundamental solutions of the Laplacian.

fields.title: Harmonic analysis
fields.description: Fourier series, the Fourier transform on R^n, Fourier analysis on finite groups and the Boolean cube, singular integrals, and other integral transforms and moment problems.

subfields.title: Fourier series
subfields.description: Fourier series on the circle and torus: Fejér and Dirichlet kernels, pointwise and Cesàro convergence, Riemann–Lebesgue, uniqueness, absolutely convergent series and Wiener's theorems, periodic convolution, Fourier optimization on the torus.

subfields.title: Fourier transform and uncertainty principles
subfields.description: The Fourier transform on R^n and Schwartz functions: convolution, Bochner, Hausdorff–Young, Heisenberg and fractal uncertainty, band-limited functions and Bernstein inequalities, sampling and Fourier interpolation, Kakeya sets, Beurling–Ahlfors and other singular integrals.

subfields.title: Discrete Fourier analysis
subfields.description: Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups and the Boolean cube: DFT and FFT, Plancherel, finite uncertainty, Young and Hausdorff–Young, Riesz–Thorin on finite sets, influences and noise operators.

subfields.title: Integral transforms and moment problems
subfields.description: Laplace, Mellin and Radon transforms (Ramanujan's master theorem, Fourier slice theorem) and Hausdorff moment problems.

fields.title: Banach space theory
fields.description: Normed, Banach and topological vector spaces: duality, weak topologies, geometry of the unit ball, bases and classical sequence spaces.

subfields.title: Duality, weak topologies and reflexivity
subfields.description: Hahn–Banach, annihilators and bipolars, weak and weak-star convergence and topologies, Goldstine, James, Eberlein–Šmulian, Krein–Šmulian, Banach–Alaoglu, Mazur's lemma, Banach limits, Hamel bases and discontinuous functionals, F-spaces and locally convex spaces, Choquet theory.

subfields.title: Geometry of Banach spaces
subfields.description: Convexity and smoothness of norms (uniform convexity, Kadec–Klee, Birkhoff–James), extreme points of balls, Auerbach and Schauder bases, approximation property, isometries (Banach–Stone, Mazur–Ulam), Banach–Mazur, Dvoretzky–Rogers, Grothendieck, Rademacher type, Daugavet, Bishop–Phelps.

subfields.title: Classical sequence spaces
subfields.description: ℓ^p and c₀: duality, Schauder bases, compactness criteria, Schur and Rosenthal ℓ¹ theorems, Pitt's theorem, quotients of ℓ¹, finite ℓ^p geometry, convolution on ℓ^p(ℤ).

fields.title: Hilbert spaces
fields.description: Geometry of inner product spaces: nearest-point projections, orthonormal and Hilbert bases, separability and ℓ², frames and Riesz bases, weak convergence (Opial, Radon–Riesz), Kirszbraun extension, derivatives of the norm, representer theorems; operators on Hilbert spaces go to Operator theory, analytic RKHS to Complex analysis.

fields.title: Operator theory
fields.description: Bounded linear operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces: spectra, compact and Fredholm operators, shifts and other concrete operators, and eigenvalue inequalities.

subfields.title: Spectral theory
subfields.description: Spectra and spectral theorems: self-adjoint, normal and compact self-adjoint spectral theorems, approximate and essential spectrum, numerical range and radius, Cayley transform, spectra of finite-rank and rank-one operators, almost Mathieu operator.

subfields.title: Compact and Fredholm operators
subfields.description: Compact and finite-rank operators, Schauder's theorem, complete continuity, Hilbert–Schmidt operators, Riesz–Schauder theory, Fredholm alternative and index, closed-range theorems.

subfields.title: Bounded operators and operator topologies
subfields.description: General bounded operators: Douglas lemma, direct sums, strong and weak operator convergence, uniform boundedness, Hellinger–Toeplitz, invariant subspaces (Lomonosov), hypercyclicity criteria, Wold decomposition.

subfields.title: Shift, Toeplitz and Hankel operators
subfields.description: Unilateral, bilateral and weighted shifts and their spectra, indices and numerical ranges, Rolewicz backward shifts, Toeplitz, Hankel and composition operators on ℓ².

subfields.title: Integral, multiplication and diagonal operators
subfields.description: Volterra and kernel integral operators, Cesàro and Hilbert operators, multiplication operators on C(X) and L², diagonal operators, Schur tests, L^p bounds for integral operators.

subfields.title: Eigenvalue inequalities and perturbation
subfields.description: Courant–Fischer, Weyl, Ky Fan, Cauchy interlacing, Schur–Horn, Eckart–Young, Bauer–Fike, Peierls–Klein for self-adjoint operators; statements only about finite matrices move to LinearAlgebra.

fields.title: Banach and operator algebras
fields.description: Banach algebras and C*- and von Neumann algebras: exponentials and product formulas in Banach algebras, GNS, Gelfand–Naimark, bicommutant, Kaplansky density, Russo–Dye, Stinespring, Kadison–Singer and the Marcus–Spielman–Srivastava theorem.

fields.title: Function spaces and Sobolev inequalities
fields.description: L^p and Sobolev spaces of functions: embeddings (Morrey, Rellich, radial, trace), Ehrling, Agmon, Ladyzhenskaya, Gagliardo–Nirenberg and weighted Hardy–Sobolev inequalities, sup-norm bounds by H¹ energy, L^p limits and weak convergence in L^p.

fields.title: Distributions
fields.description: Test functions, Schwartz functions, tempered distributions and distributional derivatives: principal values, Plemelj limits, Dirac comb, partitions of unity.

fields.title: Ordinary differential equations
fields.description: Existence and uniqueness (Cauchy–Peano, Picard, maximal solutions), linear systems and fundamental matrices, stability and Lyapunov's indirect method, Sturm–Liouville and boundary value problems with their Green's operators and eigenfunctions, oscillation and comparison theorems.

fields.title: Partial differential equations
fields.description: PDE existence, regularity and qualitative results: Cauchy–Kovalevskaya, heat and Airy equations, Euler singularity formation, σ₂ Hessian estimates, radial symmetry, viscosity solutions, Dirichlet and Neumann spectra of the Laplacian.

fields.title: Convex analysis and calculus of variations
fields.description: Convex functions and sets in analysis and optimization: Fenchel conjugates, polar sets, Moreau decomposition, convex projections, KKT conditions, gradient descent rates, Stampacchia, Tikhonov regularization, Euler–Lagrange, mountain pass and Ekeland principles; linear programming goes to convex geometry.

fields.title: Fixed-point theory
fields.description: Fixed points of nonexpansive, Lipschitz and affine maps: the Browder–Göhde–Kirk theorem and Kirk's normal structure, Markov–Kakutani, Browder's demiclosedness principle, maps with contracting iterates.

fields.title: Numerical analysis
fields.description: Algorithms with error analysis: bisection and Newton's method, Euler and Runge–Kutta methods, Galerkin and finite element estimates (Céa, Aubin–Nitsche, Strang, Banach–Nečas–Babuška).

fields.title: Approximation theory
fields.description: Approximation and interpolation of functions: Chebyshev equioscillation, best approximation, Lagrange interpolation, Bernstein polynomials and Voronovskaya, Korovkin, Müntz–Szász, Runge, Kolmogorov superposition, universal approximation.

Biology.title: Mathematical Biology
Biology.description: Mathematical biology models populations, genomes, and biochemical networks, from coalescents and reaction dynamics to the algorithms that read biological sequences.

fields.title: Population genetics
fields.description: Mathematical models of allele frequencies in populations under random mating, selection, mutation, migration and genetic drift, including the Wright–Fisher and Moran models and their diffusion limits.

subfields.title: Diffusion theory
subfields.description: The Wright–Fisher diffusion as the continuum limit of allele-frequency dynamics: generator and semigroup, fixation probabilities, absorption and sojourn times, mutation and stationary laws, allele age and the Poisson random field.

fields.title: Coalescent theory
fields.description: Backward-in-time models of the genealogy of a sample of genes, from Kingman's coalescent and its generalizations to the site frequency spectrum, recombination and population structure.

fields.title: Detecting natural selection
fields.description: Statistical tests of neutrality and genome scans for selection based on polymorphism, divergence and haplotype structure, and models of the distribution of fitness effects.

fields.title: Population structure and admixture
fields.description: f-statistics, admixture graphs, ancestry models and linkage-disequilibrium methods for inferring the relationships and mixture histories of populations.

fields.title: Phylogenetics
fields.description: Reconstruction of evolutionary trees from sequence data: substitution models, likelihood and parsimony, distance methods, tree metrics, splits and the enumeration of phylogenetic trees.

fields.title: Quantitative genetics
fields.description: The genetics of continuously varying traits: decomposition of genetic variance, resemblance between relatives, kinship, mixed models and the response to selection.

fields.title: Statistical genetics
fields.description: Statistical methods for genome-wide association studies, heritability estimation from summary statistics, fine-mapping, Mendelian randomization and gene constraint scores.

fields.title: Cancer genomics
fields.description: Mathematical models for tumour sequencing data: purity and copy number, cancer cell fractions, mutation detection power, mutational signatures and the timing of genomic events.

fields.title: Bioinformatics
fields.description: Algorithms and statistical models on biological sequences and data: sequence alignment, genome assembly, motifs, RNA secondary structure, clustering and network reconstruction.

subfields.title: Sequence alignment
subfields.description: Pairwise and multiple alignment of biological sequences: Needleman–Wunsch and Smith–Waterman, affine gaps, banded, linear-space, semi-global and wavefront algorithms.

fields.title: Systems biology
fields.description: Dynamics of biochemical reaction networks and gene regulatory circuits: mass-action kinetics, enzyme kinetics, ultrasensitivity, feedback, metabolic flux analysis and gene expression noise.

fields.title: Population and evolutionary dynamics
fields.description: Differential-equation models of population growth, species interaction and evolutionary change, such as logistic growth, predator–prey systems, replicator dynamics and quasispecies.

fields.title: Reaction–diffusion and pattern formation
fields.description: Reaction–diffusion models of biological spread and spatial patterning, including travelling waves, morphogen gradients and Turing instabilities.

fields.title: Mathematical epidemiology
fields.description: Compartmental, renewal and branching-process models of infectious disease transmission and their reproduction numbers.

CategoryTheory.title: Category Theory
CategoryTheory.description: Category theory organizes mathematical structures through morphisms, functors, universal properties, limits, and adjunctions.

fields.title: Monoidal categories
fields.description: Monoidal categories equip a category with a tensor product and unit object, with braided and symmetric variants governing how tensor factors may be exchanged.

fields.title: Topos theory
fields.description: Topos theory studies elementary and Grothendieck toposes, categories with finite limits, exponentials and a subobject classifier that behave like universes of sets.

fields.title: Homological algebra
fields.description: Homological algebra studies abelian categories through projective resolutions and the derived functors they define, such as Tor, together with their additivity.

Combinatorics.title: Combinatorics
Combinatorics.description: Combinatorics studies finite and discrete configurations through counting, extremal structure, and constructive arguments.

fields.title: Binomial coefficients and identities
fields.description: Binomial, multinomial and generalized binomial coefficients and closed-form evaluation of finite sums built from them (alternating, reciprocal, harmonic-weighted, hypergeometric), including Apéry-like sequences such as Franel, Domb and Zagier numbers; q-binomials go to symmetric functions and q-analogues, Catalan-type numbers to Catalan numbers, Stirling-weighted sums to Stirling numbers.

subfields.title: Binomial sums and hypergeometric identities
subfields.description: Evaluations and bounds of sums of products of binomial coefficients: Chu–Vandermonde, Dixon, Knuth's old sum, Staver, Frisch, Klamkin, hockey-stick and Filipponi identities, partial-sum bounds, multisection identities, and Franel, Domb, Zagier and Catalan–Larcombe–French numbers defined by binomial sums.

subfields.title: Central binomial coefficients and harmonic sums
subfields.description: Finite sums and power series involving central binomial coefficients or their reciprocals, often weighted by harmonic or odd harmonic numbers, including arcsin-type series and Kollár's incomplete binomial sums.

subfields.title: Generalized binomial coefficients and Pascal-like triangles
subfields.description: Variants of the binomial coefficient and of Pascal's triangle: b-ary and digital (carry-free) binomial coefficients, Ward and totienomial coefficients from generalized factorials, trinomial and quadrinomial coefficients, rascal, hyperbolic Pascal and 2-Pascal triangles and their diagonals; the Pascal matrix viewed as a Riordan array goes to Riordan arrays.

fields.title: Catalan numbers and lattice paths
fields.description: The Catalan family of counting sequences and the lattice paths they count: Catalan, Fuss–Catalan, Narayana, Motzkin, Schröder, Fine and Riordan numbers, Dyck and Motzkin paths and their statistics, Delannoy numbers and walks with prescribed steps, including arithmetic properties (parity, integrality, perfect powers) of these numbers.

subfields.title: Catalan numbers and their generalizations
subfields.description: Catalan numbers and generalizations defined by formulas or recurrences: Fuss–Catalan, super Catalan, (p,q)-Patalan, Whitt and Sabar arrays, generalized Catalan–Schröder, Fine and Riordan numbers, Narayana numbers and polynomials, Touchard's identity, Raney's cycle lemma, and divisibility or growth of these numbers.

subfields.title: Motzkin numbers and Motzkin paths
subfields.description: Motzkin numbers and paths: colored, weighted and (u,l,d) Motzkin paths, humps and peaks, the Motzkin triangle, links with central trinomial coefficients, alternating Motzkin sums, Aigner's inequality, and Motzkin-related sequences such as A005773; weighted Motzkin paths used to compute Hankel determinants go to Hankel determinants and continued fractions.

subfields.title: Dyck paths and lattice walks
subfields.description: Statistics on Dyck paths (peaks, valleys, marked steps, subwords) and their variants (skew, rational, k-box Dyck paths), lattice walks with unit or diagonal steps, Delannoy numbers, Sulanke arrays, colored Dyck paths, and nonintersecting paths via the Lindström–Gessel–Viennot lemma.

fields.title: Stirling, Bell and Eulerian numbers
fields.description: The number triangles and sequences that count set partitions, permutations by cycles, descents and excedances, and their relatives: Stirling and Lah numbers and their generalizations, Bell and Fubini numbers and Bell polynomials, Eulerian numbers and polynomials, and Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers studied combinatorially.

subfields.title: Stirling and Lah numbers
subfields.description: Classical Stirling numbers of the first and second kind and Lah numbers: recurrences, explicit and addition formulas, rising and falling factorial expansions, orthogonality and inverse Stirling matrices, cycle counts, inequalities and identities such as Lee's and Gy's.

subfields.title: Generalized Stirling numbers
subfields.description: Deformations and generalizations of Stirling numbers: r-Stirling, associated Stirling, Hsu–Shiue, Jacobi–Stirling, Legendre–Stirling, meromorphic and degenerate Stirling numbers, α-Stirling and generalized Stirling matrices, and (q,r)-Whitney and Dowling numbers.

subfields.title: Bell numbers, Fubini numbers and Bell polynomials
subfields.description: Bell numbers (Dobinski, Spivey, Touchard and Turán-type identities, log-convexity), complete, partial and generalized Bell polynomials, potential polynomials, Fubini (ordered Bell) numbers and their congruences, and horse numbers.

subfields.title: Eulerian numbers and polynomials
subfields.description: Counting permutations by descents or excedances: Eulerian numbers and polynomials, refined, multiset and generalized Eulerian polynomials, associated Stirling–Eulerian numbers, Worpitzky's identity, gamma-positivity and Hankel determinants of Eulerian polynomials, Bell permutations by weak excedances.

subfields.title: Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers
subfields.description: Combinatorial formulas for Bernoulli, Euler, tangent and Genocchi numbers (Garabedian's formulas, median Euler and Genocchi numbers, Euler–Seidel matrices, Carlitz q-Bernoulli polynomials), their divisibility, and sums of powers via Faulhaber coefficients.

fields.title: Riordan arrays and sequence transforms
fields.description: Infinite lower-triangular arrays and operators on sequences studied through generating functions: the Riordan group, number triangles and their diagonals, binomial, INVERT and Catalan transforms, Hankel and Toeplitz determinants and continued fractions; a specific named family (Motzkin triangle, Stirling matrices) stays with that family.

subfields.title: Riordan arrays and number triangles
subfields.description: Riordan arrays and their A- and Z-sequences, inverses, triple factorizations, pseudo-involutions and total positivity, the Pascal and Pell matrices as Riordan arrays, Barry's triangles, triangular recurrence arrays extended to negative rows, and diagonal or row sums of triangles.

subfields.title: Hankel determinants and continued fractions
subfields.description: Hankel transforms of sequences and their invariance under binomial transforms, Heilermann's formula linking Jacobi continued fractions to weighted Motzkin paths, Catalan-sum Hankel determinants, and Toeplitz–Hessenberg determinants.

subfields.title: Sequence transforms and generating functions
subfields.description: Operators on integer sequences and coefficient extraction: binomial, multiple and falling k-binomial transforms, INVERT and Catalan transforms, hypersequences, convolutions, C-finite sequences, and recovering terms from generating-function values.

fields.title: Integer partitions
fields.description: Partitions of integers as combinatorial objects: identities equating partition counts and their bijective proofs, Young diagrams and partition statistics, and counting partitions; congruences for partition functions and theta- or eta-quotient identities go to NumberTheory.

subfields.title: Partition identities
subfields.description: Theorems equating counts of two classes of partitions: Euler, MacMahon, Andrews, Andrews–Lewis, Rogers–Ramanujan, Stanley and Elder theorems, polarized and 2-distant partitions, colored Euler-type identities and Merca's sums of different parts.

subfields.title: Young diagrams and partition statistics
subfields.description: Statistics and structure of a single partition: conjugation, hook lengths, s-cores, perimeter, diagonal sequences, lit cells, rank and crank, max-rook numbers, perfect and double-perfect partitions, and reconstruction of a partition from pairwise products.

subfields.title: Counting partitions
subfields.description: The partition function and its relatives as counts: bounds and asymptotics for p(n), the pentagonal number theorem, partition polynomials, Landau's function, overpartitions and regular partitions counted (not their congruences), restricted Gaussian and bounded partitions.

fields.title: Integer compositions
fields.description: Ordered sums of positive integers: compositions with restricted, palindromic, colored or n-color parts, Arndt compositions, perfect compositions, shade, symmetric peaks and valleys, and convolution identities for weighted compositions.

fields.title: Permutations
fields.description: Permutations of a finite set as combinatorial objects: pattern containment and avoidance, and statistics and cycle structure; descent-counting numbers go to Eulerian numbers, Stirling cycle numbers to Stirling numbers.

subfields.title: Permutation patterns
subfields.description: Classical, consecutive, mesh and signed patterns in permutations and in inversion and ascent sequences, pattern-avoidance counts, pattern-replacement classes, stack sorting, and king and separable permutations.

subfields.title: Permutation statistics and cycle structure
subfields.description: Descents, peaks, major index, left-to-right maxima, fixed points and derangements, cycle counts and the smallest cycle of a random permutation, products of cyclic permutations, Stirling and flattened Stirling permutations, Josephus permutations and permutation-guessing puzzles.

fields.title: Set partitions
fields.description: Partitions of a finite set into blocks: finite partition API, ordered and cyclic set partitions, restricted-growth words, peaks and rises, noncrossing partitions, merging-free and marriageable-singles partitions, genus of a partition, and linear chord diagrams and hypermonopoles.

fields.title: Parking functions
fields.description: Parking functions and their variants (partial, weakly increasing, k-Naples, metered) and statistics on them: lucky cars, descents, displacement, and lucky statistics of Stirling permutations read as parking preferences.

fields.title: Tilings, dimers and board placements
fields.description: Covering and placement problems on lattices and boards: domino and lozenge tilings and perfect matchings of grid regions (Aztec diamonds, Möbius grids, cylinders and tori), polyominoes and polycubes, tilings of groups by translates and the periodic tiling conjecture, nonattacking chess pieces, rook and file placements on Ferrers boards, and self-avoiding walks on lattices.

fields.title: Symmetric functions, tableaux and q-analogues
fields.description: Algebraic combinatorics of symmetric functions and Young tableaux, Gaussian binomial coefficients and other q-analogues, alternating sign matrices and plane partitions (q-TSPP, Robbins numbers), Coxeter–Catalan positivity, chromatic symmetric functions, minuscule polynomials, and positivity or real-rootedness of permanents and gamma vectors.

fields.title: Combinatorics on words
fields.description: Finite and infinite words over finite alphabets: repetitions and avoidability, morphic and Sturmian words, factor complexity, automatic and regular sequences, Lyndon and primitive words, and integer sequences defined by self-description or self-generation.

subfields.title: Repetitions in words
subfields.description: Squares, overlaps, cubes and fractional powers in words: square-free and overlap-free words, abelian and k-abelian repetitions, power-free morphisms, Crochemore's test and Dejean's repetition threshold.

subfields.title: Morphic and Sturmian words
subfields.description: Infinite words generated by substitutions and their codings: Fibonacci, Tribonacci and Thue–Morse words and generalizations, pure morphic and morphic words, Sturmian and balanced words, factor complexity and Pansiot's classification, palindromic and relative-position properties, first differences of binary words.

subfields.title: Automatic sequences and numeration systems
subfields.description: k-automatic and k-regular sequences, Cobham's theorem and kernels, meta-automatic sequences, results proved with the Walnut prover, and numeration systems (Dumont–Thomas, Tribonacci and Zeckendorf representations) whose digit words define such sequences.

subfields.title: Finite words
subfields.description: Properties of finite words: Lyndon and primitive words, equilibrious words, Ulam words, keyword substitutions, universal cycles for subsets, capacity of Catalan words, rectangles in nondecreasing words, and intersections in pairs of words.

subfields.title: Self-describing and self-generating sequences
subfields.description: Integer sequences defined by self-reference, greedy or mex rules: Kolakoski, Gijswijt (curling numbers), Cloitre, Connell, Aronson, Smarandache, van der Laan, throwback and anti-recurrence sequences, self-generating sets, fractal sequences and inventory loops.

fields.title: Additive combinatorics
fields.description: The additive structure of sets in integers and abelian groups: sumsets and inverse theorems, sum-product growth, Sidon sets and difference sets, sum-free sets, additive bases, zero-sum problems, and arithmetic progressions in dense sets; colouring (Ramsey-type) versions go to Ramsey theory.

subfields.title: Sumsets and inverse theorems
subfields.description: Size and structure of A+B, hA and restricted or signed sumsets: Cauchy–Davenport and Vosper, Freiman-type and polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa theorems, small doubling, sums of dilates, h-fold sumsets with distinct terms, rectification, sets determined by k-sums, max-min (lunar) decompositions, and sum-product and product-set growth.

subfields.title: Sets with more sums than differences
subfields.description: Comparison of |A+A| with |A−A|: sum-dominant (MSTD) and difference-dominated sets, minimal MSTD and MPTQ sets, Chu's constructions, unions of progressions, and the single-set sum-difference exponent.

subfields.title: Sidon sets and difference sets
subfields.description: Sidon and B_h-sets (bounds, counts, greedy and thick constructions, isolated sums, the Sidon ideal), Golomb rulers, difference bases, cyclic and perfect difference sets including Singer's theorem, and difference sets of sparse sets.

subfields.title: Sum-free sets
subfields.description: Sets with no solution to x+y=z or similar: sum-free sets in abelian groups and intervals, counts of sum-free and maximal sum-free sets, large sum-free subsets, square-sum-free, divisor-sum-free and non-averaging sets.

subfields.title: Additive bases
subfields.description: Sets whose h-fold sums cover the integers or a group: asymptotic, exact and restricted bases, Schnirelmann density, Rohrbach's theorem, representation counts and convolutions, sums of cubes covering vector spaces, knight-move bases of the plane, and sumsets of infinite sets of positive or zero density.

subfields.title: Zero-sum problems and subset sums
subfields.description: Davenport and weighted Davenport constants, zero-sum subsequences and cross numbers, Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv-type results, perfect subset-sum covers, zero subset sums and balanced subset sums in finite abelian groups, and subset sums with bounded numbers of terms.

subfields.title: Arithmetic progressions in dense sets
subfields.description: Density versions: Szemerédi's and Roth's theorems and Roth-number bounds, Sárközy's theorem, cap sets, counts of three-term progressions, progressions in complements and in walks, arithmetic progression API, and polynomial triangle removal in vector spaces.

fields.title: Ramsey theory
fields.description: Unavoidable monochromatic structure under finite colourings of integers, words, sets and semigroups; graph and ordered-graph Ramsey problems go to GraphTheory, ordinal and infinite-cardinal partition relations to SetTheory, density statements without colouring to additive combinatorics.

subfields.title: Van der Waerden-type theorems
subfields.description: Monochromatic arithmetic progressions: van der Waerden's theorem and van der Waerden numbers (off-diagonal, W(3,k)), short or large-difference progressions, rainbow progressions, descending waves, accessible sets and diffsequences, and progression-free Ramsey sets.

subfields.title: Schur and Rado theorems
subfields.description: Monochromatic solutions of equations: Schur's theorem and Schur and modular Schur numbers, Rado's theorem and disjunctive Rado, monochromatic linear equations, monochromatic sums, sums of squares and products, and rainbow-free colourings of x−y=z^k.

subfields.title: Ramsey's theorem, Hales–Jewett and Hindman
subfields.description: Ramsey's theorem for sets and hypergraphs (including size Ramsey numbers and Paris–Harrington), Hales–Jewett and density Hales–Jewett, Hindman's and the pairwise sum theorem via ultrafilters, central, J-, C- and piecewise syndetic sets in semigroups, and grid Ramsey properties.

fields.title: Extremal set theory and hypergraphs
fields.description: Largest or smallest families of finite sets under intersection, union or containment constraints, and hypergraphs (uniform set systems) studied by Turán, colouring, matching and covering parameters; problems about graphs go to GraphTheory.

subfields.title: Intersecting families, Sperner theory and sunflowers
subfields.description: Erdős–Ko–Rado and its variants, Chvátal's conjecture, forbidden and singleton intersections, comparable pairs, union-free and union-closed families, shadows (Kruskal–Katona, Macaulay), Harper's isoperimetric inequality, and sunflower bounds.

subfields.title: Hypergraph Turán problems
subfields.description: Turán numbers and densities of uniform hypergraphs: Turán systems, de Caen's question, generalized triangles, the (6,3) problem, locally sparse triple systems, and dense 3-uniform hypergraphs.

subfields.title: Hypergraph colouring, matchings and covers
subfields.description: Property B and hypergraph colouring, Erdős–Faber–Lovász, Kneser hypergraphs, independence in Steiner and linear triple systems, set mappings, strongly maximal matchings, minimal covers, transversals, Baranyai's theorem and common elements of small set families.

fields.title: Designs, Latin squares and combinatorial matrices
fields.description: Block designs, Steiner systems, pairwise balanced designs and linear spaces, Latin squares and transversals, Hadamard and partial Hadamard matrices, magic squares, 0-1 matrices with prescribed margins (Gale–Ryser), binary matrices up to rotation, and sign tables from determinant-moment expansions; cyclic difference sets go to Sidon sets and difference sets.

fields.title: Matroid theory
fields.description: Matroids and their invariants: algebraic matroids, Edmonds' intersection and partition theorems, Rado's theorem, characteristic polynomials and log-concavity, the Mason conjectures, Lorentzian polynomials, and lines in weighted matroids.

fields.title: Partially ordered sets
fields.description: Finite posets as combinatorial objects: Dilworth's and Mirsky's theorems, Erdős–Szekeres monotone subsequences, linear extensions, Möbius algebras and flag vectors, chain polynomials and Neggers' conjecture, Sperner properties of the weak order, rowmotion and toggle homomesy, poset matrices and rooted trees; lattice theory goes to Order.

fields.title: Polytopes, Ehrhart theory and simplicial complexes
fields.description: Face numbers and h-vectors of simplicial spheres and polytopes (Dehn–Sommerville, upper bound theorem), Cohen–Macaulay, partitionable and interval-decomposable complexes, simplicial homology, Ehrhart polynomials, h*-vectors and the integer decomposition property, lattice parallelograms, and hyperplane arrangements.

fields.title: Discrepancy theory
fields.description: How evenly a set system, matrix or vector family can be two-coloured: matrix and vector discrepancy, the Komlós and Beck–Fiala problems, hereditary discrepancy, vector balancing, balanced weighted colourings and balancing infinite families.

fields.title: Probabilistic combinatorics
fields.description: Probabilistic methods and random discrete structures outside random graphs: the Lovász local lemma, Littlewood–Offord and Tomaszewski anti-concentration for signed sums, concentration of subset sums, the isolation lemma, thresholds and expectation thresholds, random k-SAT thresholds, perfect matchings in random hypergraphs, the Chvátal–Sankoff constant for longest common subsequences, and moment-based counting bounds.

fields.title: Boolean functions
fields.description: Functions from {0,1}^n to {0,1}: counting monotone, self-dual and unate Boolean functions and Dedekind numbers, enumeration of k-SAT functions, noise stability and juntas, and parity and small-bias counts over finite fields.

fields.title: Elementary enumeration
fields.description: Counting basic objects under simple constraints: subsets, multisets and functions with prescribed values, Schreier-type and weighted Schreier sets, combinations avoiding given differences, necklaces and counting up to rotation, fibre and double counting, introductory catalogues of special counting sequences, and small extremal puzzles such as the bridge and torch problem.

ComputerScience.title: Computer Science
ComputerScience.description: Computer science formalizes algorithms, programming-language structures, data abstractions, and correctness properties.

fields.title: Data structures
fields.description: Representations of collections with their invariants, operations and costs (worst-case and amortized), whether the structure is developed on its own or as an augmented variant; an algorithm that merely uses a structure goes to the field of the problem it solves.

subfields.title: Search trees and skip lists
subfields.description: Ordered dictionaries: binary search trees and their balanced variants (AVL, red-black, 2-3, B-trees, splay, treaps, weight-balanced, Cartesian, order-statistic) and skip lists, including their insertion and deletion procedures.

subfields.title: Heaps and priority queues
subfields.description: Priority queues: binary, d-ary, binomial, Fibonacci and catenable heaps, indexed min-queues, and their sift, decrease-key and merge operations and costs.

subfields.title: Hashing
subfields.description: Hash tables (chaining, open addressing, cuckoo, perfect), universal hash families and Bloom filters including their false-positive analysis.

subfields.title: Lists, stacks, queues and dynamic arrays
subfields.description: Sequential containers and their amortized costs: linked lists (singly, doubly, sentinel), stacks with multipop, queues, deques, dynamic tables, binary counters, LRU caches, and generic list operations (ordered insertion, splitting, chunking, inclusive prefixes) that support them.

subfields.title: Range-query and spatial structures
subfields.description: Structures answering range, interval or nearest-point queries: segment trees, Fenwick trees, sparse tables, interval trees, range trees, kd-trees, ball trees and fractional cascading.

subfields.title: Tries, suffix structures and integer dictionaries
subfields.description: Prefix- and bit-indexed structures: tries, radix (Patricia) tries, suffix arrays and suffix trees, van Emde Boas trees, x-fast and y-fast tries.

subfields.title: Disjoint sets and dynamic trees
subfields.description: Union-find with rank and path compression (including its connected-components application), link-cut trees and Euler-tour trees.

fields.title: Graph algorithms
fields.description: Algorithms computing properties of explicit graphs (traversal, connectivity, shortest paths, spanning trees, flows, matchings, Euler circuits) with correctness and cost proofs; pure graph theory belongs to GraphTheory, and verifiers or reductions for NP problems belong to TheoryOfComputation.

subfields.title: Graph traversal and connectivity
subfields.description: Graph representations as adjacency lists and adjacency matrices, breadth-first and depth-first search with predecessor trees, strongly connected components, topological sorting, transitive closure and Hierholzer's Euler circuits.

subfields.title: Shortest paths
subfields.description: Single-source and all-pairs shortest paths: Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, DAG relaxation, min-plus matrix products and APSP, Floyd-Warshall and Johnson.

subfields.title: Spanning trees, flows and matchings
subfields.description: Minimum spanning trees (Kruskal, Prim), maximum flow and minimum cut (Edmonds-Karp), bipartite matching by augmenting paths, and Gale-Shapley stable matching.

fields.title: Sorting and searching
fields.description: Comparison and distribution sorting algorithms (including their expected-cost analyses), and searching and selection in lists and arrays (binary and linear search, quickselect, median of medians, simultaneous min-max). Comparator sorting networks, their depth and the 0-1 principle form the Sorting networks subfield.

subfields.title: Sorting networks
subfields.description: Comparator networks that sort: the bubble network, Batcher's bitonic and odd–even merge networks, depth bounds, and the zero-one and permutation principles.

fields.title: Dynamic programming
fields.description: Optimization problems solved by tabulated recurrences: knapsack variants, subset sum, rod cutting, matrix-chain ordering, optimal binary search trees, longest common and longest increasing subsequences (including patience sorting) and maximum subarray (Kadane and divide-and-conquer); string edit distance goes to String algorithms.

fields.title: Greedy algorithms and matroids
fields.description: Greedy choice and exchange arguments: the matroid greedy algorithm and its characterization of matroids, graphic matroids, interval scheduling and furthest-in-future offline caching.

fields.title: Approximation algorithms
fields.description: Polynomial-time algorithms with proved approximation ratios for NP-hard optimization: vertex cover, set cover, metric TSP, list scheduling, maximum coverage.

fields.title: Online algorithms
fields.description: Algorithms that act on a request sequence without knowing the future, and competitive-ratio upper and lower bounds: paging, list update, ski rental, online bipartite matching.

fields.title: Randomized algorithms and probabilistic analysis
fields.description: Algorithms whose identity is their use of randomness or whose analysis averages over random inputs: expected running time under input distributions, Fisher-Yates shuffling, the hiring problem, Karger's minimum cut, Freivalds' matrix-product check and MinHash similarity sketches.

fields.title: Parallel algorithms
fields.description: Work-span models, Brent's theorem and greedy scheduling, parallel prefix sums (Blelloch, Kogge-Stone) and pointer-jumping list ranking.

fields.title: Algebraic and numerical algorithms
fields.description: Algorithms on numbers, polynomials and matrices: integer and polynomial multiplication (Karatsuba, FFT and convolution), matrix multiplication (iterative, recursive, Strassen), Horner evaluation, floating-point rounding, modular exponentiation and linear congruences, Miller-Rabin primality testing, and bit-level polynomial and bitvector arithmetic.

fields.title: Computational geometry
fields.description: Algorithms on points and segments in the plane: orientation and segment intersection, sweep-line intersection detection, convex hulls and closest pair; geometric search structures stay in Data structures.

fields.title: String algorithms
fields.description: Exact pattern matching (naive, finite automaton, Knuth-Morris-Pratt, Boyer-Moore, Rabin-Karp, Z algorithm) and edit distance with edit scripts; biological sequence alignment belongs to Biology.

fields.title: Heuristic search and planning
fields.description: Search and decision procedures from artificial intelligence: A* search, game-tree search with alpha-beta pruning, arc consistency for constraint satisfaction, and value and policy iteration for Markov decision processes.

fields.title: Cryptography
fields.description: Cryptographic schemes and their correctness and security reductions: public-key encryption and key agreement, signatures, identification protocols, pseudorandom functions, perfect secrecy and hash-function constructions including the birthday bound.

fields.title: Databases
fields.description: Relational algebra, functional dependencies, normal forms and lossless decomposition, and transaction concurrency control (conflict serializability, two-phase locking).

fields.title: Quantum algorithms
fields.description: Algorithms for quantum computers and their analysis: Grover search and the classical order-to-factor core of Shor's algorithm.

fields.title: Process calculi and behavioural equivalence
fields.description: Algebraic models of concurrent processes: labelled transition systems and their runs, strong and weak bisimulation, observational congruence, CCS (choice, parallel composition, restriction, recursion, finite-state agents) and the pi-calculus.

subfields.title: Session types
subfields.description: Session types for the π-calculus: binary protocols and their duality, linear endpoint typing with ownership contexts, subject reduction, progress by priorities, typing up to protocol equivalence, and shared and recursive services.

fields.title: Concurrent systems and protocols
fields.description: Specific concurrent or distributed systems and their verified properties: deadlock and its detection, the banker's algorithm, dining philosophers, and communication protocols such as the alternating-bit protocol and go-back-N.

fields.title: Programming language semantics
fields.description: Operational and denotational semantics of programming languages and correctness of compilation: the IMP language (syntax, big- and small-step, heap semantics, denotational semantics, stack-machine compilation), PCF with adequacy and contextual equivalence, CPS translation and closure conversion.

fields.title: Type systems and lambda calculi
fields.description: Typed lambda calculi and type inference: the simply typed lambda calculus (syntax, substitution, normalization, logical relations, normalization by evaluation, elaboration, its models), lambda calculus with references and type safety, and Hindley-Milner let-polymorphism with Algorithm W.

fields.title: Program logics and verification
fields.description: Logics for proving programs correct: Hoare logic for partial and total correctness with soundness and relative completeness, weakest preconditions, verification-condition generation, and separation logic.

fields.title: Machine learning
fields.description: Mathematical theory of learning from data, including the probabilistic modelling, inference and sampling methods used in machine learning.

subfields.title: Online learning and boosting
subfields.description: Mistake and regret bounds for sequential prediction: perceptron, weighted majority, Hedge (multiplicative weights) and AdaBoost.

subfields.title: Supervised learning and regression
subfields.description: Prediction from labelled data: least squares, ridge, lasso and kernel or Gaussian-process regression (including GBLUP), the bias-variance decomposition, Bayes classifiers and optimal predictors, log loss, decision-tree information gain, backpropagation, and sufficient input subsets.

subfields.title: Unsupervised learning and matrix factorization
subfields.description: Structure in unlabelled data: k-means, archetypal analysis, nonnegative matrix factorization, the successive projection algorithm and probabilistic PCA.

subfields.title: Probabilistic graphical models
subfields.description: Bayesian networks and their Markov properties, structure scores and Markov equivalence, causal networks and adjustment, belief propagation and variable elimination, conditional random fields, hidden Markov models (forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch) and the Kalman filter.

subfields.title: Bayesian inference and sampling
subfields.description: Bayes' rule and conjugate models, expectation-maximization for mixtures and latent-variable models, variational mean-field inference, and Monte Carlo, rejection, Gibbs and Metropolis-Hastings sampling.

Dynamics.title: Dynamical Systems
Dynamics.description: Dynamics studies systems evolving through iteration or time, including recurrence, stability, and long-term behavior.

fields.title: Ergodic theory
fields.description: Ergodic theory studies measure-preserving transformations and their statistical behaviour: ergodic averages, recurrence, mixing and the structure of measure-preserving actions.

fields.title: Topological and symbolic dynamics
fields.description: Topological dynamics studies continuous maps of topological spaces through orbits, periodic points and recurrence, and symbolic dynamics studies shift spaces and cellular automata on sequences of symbols.

fields.title: Low-dimensional dynamics
fields.description: Low-dimensional dynamics covers maps of the interval and circle, continued-fraction-type maps, flows in the plane and homeomorphisms of surfaces.

fields.title: Smooth dynamics
fields.description: Smooth dynamics studies differentiable maps and flows: hyperbolicity, stable manifolds and shadowing, Lyapunov exponents and entropy, Hamiltonian perturbation theory, and stability of flows given by differential equations.

fields.title: Complex dynamics
fields.description: Complex dynamics studies the iteration of holomorphic maps, especially polynomials, together with their Julia sets and parameter spaces such as the Mandelbrot set.

FieldTheory.title: Field Theory
FieldTheory.description: Field theory studies extensions of fields, algebraic elements, automorphisms, and Galois-theoretic structure.

fields.title: Galois theory
fields.description: Galois theory relates a field extension to its group of automorphisms, covering the Galois correspondence, infinite Galois groups, Hilbert's theorem 90, solvability by radicals and essential dimension.

fields.title: Finite fields
fields.description: Finite fields and polynomials over them: irreducible and primitive polynomials, permutation polynomials, and the arithmetic of squares.

fields.title: Field extensions and algebraic closure
fields.description: Algebraic field extensions and closures: minimal polynomials, separable and purely inseparable extensions, base change to separably closed fields, algebraic closures of series fields and quasi-algebraically closed fields.

GameTheory.title: Game Theory
GameTheory.description: Game theory studies strategic and combinatorial interaction, equilibria, winning conditions, and optimal play.

fields.title: Combinatorial game theory
fields.description: Combinatorial game theory studies two-player games of perfect information without chance: impartial games such as Nim and its variants (P-positions, Sprague–Grundy values, remoteness), partizan games such as Snort, and Maker–Breaker positional games.

fields.title: Cooperative game theory
fields.description: Cooperative game theory studies games in which coalitions of players can make binding agreements, and solution concepts such as the core and the Shapley value for dividing a coalition's worth.

fields.title: Social choice theory
fields.description: Social choice theory studies rules that aggregate individual preferences into a collective ranking or choice, and the impossibility theorems that limit them.

Geometry.title: Geometry
Geometry.description: Geometry studies shapes, spaces, transformations, curvature, and the invariants preserved by geometric equivalence.

fields.title: Euclidean geometry
fields.description: Classical synthetic and metric geometry of the Euclidean plane and space: triangles, circles, conics, polygons, isometries and the foundations of geometry.

subfields.title: Triangle geometry
subfields.description: Theorems about triangles, their centers, cevians, inscribed and circumscribed circles, and triangle inequalities.

subfields.title: Circles and conics
subfields.description: Configurations of circles and conics, tangency, chains of circles, lunes, and mathematical billiards in elliptic and polygonal tables.

subfields.title: Polygons and quadrilaterals
subfields.description: Theorems about quadrilaterals, cyclic polygons and squares erected on polygon sides.

subfields.title: Solid and spherical geometry
subfields.description: Metric relations for tetrahedra and other solids, and trigonometry on the sphere.

subfields.title: Isometries and crystallographic groups
subfields.description: Distance-preserving maps of Euclidean space, their classification, and discrete symmetry groups such as wallpaper and space groups.

subfields.title: Foundations and constructions
subfields.description: Axiom systems for plane geometry and the limits of compass-and-straightedge constructions.

fields.title: Convex geometry
fields.description: Convex sets and convex bodies in Euclidean space: Helly-type and Radon-type theorems, partitions, sections, valuations and linear optimization over polyhedra.

fields.title: Packings and coverings
fields.description: Optimal arrangements of congruent bodies in space and the smallest sets or fewest translates needed to cover given families of shapes.

fields.title: Discrete geometry
fields.description: Finite point configurations and their distances, polytopes and polyhedra, dissections and tilings, lattice points and extremal shape problems.

fields.title: Metric geometry
fields.description: Geometry of general metric spaces: curvature bounds via comparison, length spaces, isometric embeddings and low-distortion embeddings.

fields.title: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces
fields.description: Curvature, tangents and global properties of curves and surfaces in Euclidean space, including knotted curves and inscribed figures.

fields.title: Riemannian and Finsler geometry
fields.description: Manifolds with smoothly varying inner products or norms on tangent spaces: connections, curvature, geodesics, differential operators and rigidity theorems.

fields.title: Differential topology
fields.description: Smooth manifolds and smooth maps between them: immersions, submersions, transversality, Morse theory, neighbourhood theorems and smooth structures.

fields.title: Complex and symplectic geometry
fields.description: Manifolds with complex, almost complex, symplectic or contact structures, Riemann surfaces, and integrable Hamiltonian systems.

GraphTheory.title: Graph Theory
GraphTheory.description: Graph theory studies vertices and edges through connectivity, coloring, minors, flows, and extremal structure.

fields.title: Paths, cycles and connectivity
fields.description: Walks, paths and cycles in graphs, Eulerian and Hamiltonian cycles, and vertex and edge connectivity, including Menger's theorem and Fleischner's theorem on squares of 2-connected graphs.

fields.title: Graph coloring
fields.description: Vertex, edge, list and fractional colorings of graphs and the chromatic number, from Brooks' and Vizing's theorems to perfect graphs and the four color theorem.

fields.title: Matchings and flows
fields.description: Matchings and factors in graphs, stable matchings, and flows in networks, including Kőnig's theorem, Berge's lemma and the max-flow min-cut theorem.

fields.title: Independence, cliques and domination
fields.description: Independent sets, cliques and dominating sets in graphs, with bounds on their sizes and polynomials counting them.

fields.title: Extremal graph theory
fields.description: How many edges or copies of a subgraph a graph can have while avoiding a forbidden structure: Turán and Zarankiewicz problems, saturation, and extremal graphs of given girth.

fields.title: Ramsey theory for graphs
fields.description: Ramsey numbers of graphs, their known small values, and Ramsey–Turán problems.

fields.title: Algebraic graph theory
fields.description: Graphs studied through groups and matrices: Cayley and vertex-transitive graphs, strongly regular and Moore graphs, graph homomorphisms, Laplacians and the matrix-tree theorem, and named graphs such as the Petersen and Coxeter graphs.

fields.title: Planar graphs and minors
fields.description: Graphs drawn in the plane and on the square lattice, crossing numbers, Euler's formula, discrete Jordan curve and turning-number theorems, and the theory of graph minors.

fields.title: Graph invariants and labelings
fields.description: Numerical and polynomial invariants of graphs such as degree sequences, arboricity, induced forest number, Shannon capacity and the chromatic symmetric function, and graph labelings.

fields.title: Directed graphs and tournaments
fields.description: Directed graphs, orientations of undirected graphs, digraph colorings and tournaments.

fields.title: Graph families and operations
fields.description: Graph products, line graphs and other constructions, together with special families such as expanders and the hypercubic lattice.

fields.title: Random graphs and graph limits
fields.description: Random graph models such as Erdős–Rényi, random regular and random k-out graphs, the typical values of their invariants (chromatic number, independence ratio, connectivity, spectra), and graphons as limits of dense graph sequences.

GroupTheory.title: Group Theory
GroupTheory.description: Group theory studies symmetry through groups, actions, subgroups, quotients, and structural decompositions.

fields.title: Abelian groups
fields.description: Structure of abelian groups: finite and finitely generated abelian groups (invariant factors, elementary divisors, torsion, ranks, dual groups), torsion-free and infinite abelian groups (Baer–Specker group, pure subgroups, direct-sum cancellation, ultraproducts of abelian groups); colourings and partitions of abelian groups go to Combinatorics in groups.

fields.title: Group orders, element orders and spectra
fields.description: Arithmetic of finite groups through orders: cyclic numbers and groups of a given order (groups of order 10, dihedral groups from an index-two cyclic subgroup), counts of elements of each order, the spectrum (set of element orders), recognition of groups by spectrum or by order and spectrum, Thompson's type, and totient sums; conjugacy-class sizes go to Conjugacy classes.

fields.title: Conjugacy classes
fields.description: Conjugacy classes of groups as a structural invariant: class sizes and breadth, the class number, commuting probability, Thompson's conjecture on class sizes, products of conjugacy classes, and relations between class sizes and group structure; class sizes of p-groups go to Finite p-groups, and character-theoretic class arguments to Characters of finite groups.

fields.title: Finite simple groups and involutions
fields.description: Finite simple and almost simple groups and the local analysis behind their classification: specific simple groups (Mathieu, Suzuki, PSL), strongly embedded subgroups (Bender–Suzuki), classification by Sylow 2-subgroups (Gorenstein–Walter, Brauer–Suzuki), Baer–Suzuki, Glauberman Z*, Brauer–Fowler, involution centralizers and 3-transpositions; generation questions go to Generation of groups and spectrum recognition to Group orders, element orders and spectra.

fields.title: Generation of groups
fields.description: Minimal and special generating sets: generator numbers of almost simple and soluble groups, (2,3)-generation, generation by elements of prime-power order, spread, coprime generation, two-generated direct powers, Eulerian functions and probabilistic generation.

fields.title: Sylow and Hall subgroups
fields.description: Sylow theory and its generalization to sets of primes: Hall π-subgroups, the classes E_π, C_π and D_π, pronormality and intersections of Hall subgroups, groups whose maximal subgroups are Hall; questions on supplements of Sylow maximal subgroups forcing solubility go to Soluble and supersoluble finite groups.

fields.title: Subgroup embedding and subgroup lattices
fields.description: How subgroups sit inside a group: subnormal, permutable, propermutable, pronormal, polynormal and paranormal subgroups, maximal subgroups and their conjugates, intersections of conjugates of nilpotent subgroups and injectors with the Fitting subgroup, centralizer lattices and complemented subgroup lattices.

fields.title: Soluble and supersoluble finite groups
fields.description: Structure of finite soluble groups: supersolubility criteria, p-solubility and p-length, chief factors and their complements, σ-solubility and σ-nilpotency, Schmidt subgroups, derived length bounds for finite groups of special type, and factorized groups; classes of groups closed under operations go to Formations and Fitting classes.

subfields.title: Formations and Fitting classes
subfields.description: Classes of finite groups: formations, local and hereditary formations, Fitting and radical classes, injectors, subgroup functors, residuals, and lattices of formations; varieties defined by laws go to Varieties, quasivarieties and equations.

fields.title: Finite p-groups
fields.description: Groups of prime-power order: composition series, Frattini subgroups and Φ-extensions, special, powerful, metacyclic and Camina p-groups, conjugacy class sizes of p-groups, generalized quaternion groups, coclass and rank analogues, derived length bounds, and orders of automorphism groups of p-groups only when the p-group structure is the point.

fields.title: Characters of finite groups
fields.description: Complex characters and representations used to study finite groups: class functions and orthogonality, irreducible character bases, character degrees and values, McKay conjecture, rational groups, permutation characters, blocks of defect zero, Frobenius group determinant, convolution on finite groups, and Burnside's p^a q^b theorem; general representation theory of algebras and Lie groups belongs to RepresentationTheory.

fields.title: Permutation groups and group actions
fields.description: Groups acting on sets: orbits, stabilizers, fixed-point counts, transitivity, bases, closures, Frobenius groups, symmetric and alternating groups as permutation groups, and infinite permutation groups (highly homogeneous, cofinitary, oligomorphic, subdegree-finite).

subfields.title: Finite permutation groups
subfields.description: Actions of finite groups on finite sets: Burnside-type counting, stabilizers, multiply and doubly transitive finite groups, Frobenius groups, bases and independent sets, 2-closures, regular orbits of linear actions, coverings and products in finite symmetric groups.

subfields.title: Infinite permutation groups
subfields.description: Permutation groups on infinite sets: highly homogeneous groups of orders, circular orders and betweenness (Cameron), the pointwise topology on permutations, cofinitary and subdegree-finite groups, infinite sharply or doubly transitive groups, embeddings into the infinite symmetric group, class transpositions of the integers.

fields.title: Free groups and their automorphisms
fields.description: Free groups and free metabelian groups: subgroups (inert, compressed, retracts, fixed subgroups), elements (primitive, test, orbit-blocking words, normal closures), and the groups Aut(F_n), Out(F_n) and IA-automorphisms; equations over free groups go to Varieties, quasivarieties and equations, and commutator length to Commutators, word maps and Engel conditions.

subfields.title: Subgroups and elements of free groups
subfields.description: Subgroup and element structure inside free and free metabelian groups: rank, inertness and compressedness, derived subgroups, retracts, primitive and equally distributed elements, independent sets, separation, Cayley–Hamilton analogues and characteristic quotients.

subfields.title: Automorphisms of free groups
subfields.description: The groups Aut(F_n) and Out(F_n): fixed points and fixed subgroups of automorphisms, word problem, automaticity, linearity of IA-automorphisms, embeddings of free products into Aut(F_n).

fields.title: Presentations and decision problems
fields.description: Combinatorial group theory: presentations, one-relator groups, HNN extensions and embeddings, SQ-universality, finitely presented simple groups, the word and conjugacy problems (Novikov–Boone, Boone–Higman), Andrews–Curtis moves, generic properties of presentations and torsion quotients.

subfields.title: Braid and Artin groups
subfields.description: Braid groups, pure braid groups and Artin–Tits groups of Coxeter matrices: endomorphisms, roots, conjugators and conjugacy questions.

fields.title: Geometric group theory
fields.description: Large-scale and analytic properties of finitely generated groups: growth, word-hyperbolic groups and their quotients, amenability and Følner sets, elementary amenable groups, property (T), soficity and permutation stability.

subfields.title: Branch, automaton and Thompson groups
subfields.description: Groups acting on rooted trees, branch and just-infinite groups of intermediate growth, finite-state (automaton) groups, and Thompson's group F and its piecewise-linear relatives.

fields.title: Orderable groups
fields.description: Left-, right- and bi-orderable groups: spaces of orders, generalized torsion, unique product groups, relatively convex subgroups, orderability of homeomorphism groups and amalgams, and decision problems for orderable groups.

fields.title: Varieties, quasivarieties and equations
fields.description: Groups defined by laws and quasi-identities: varieties, relatively free groups, test ranks, quasivarieties and their lattices, Hall's verbal conjectures, plus equations over groups, equationally Noetherian groups, geometric equivalence and elementary theories of groups.

fields.title: Commutators, word maps and Engel conditions
fields.description: Commutator calculus and nilpotency in (often infinite) groups: basic commutators, Engel elements, locally nilpotent and hypercentral groups, metabelian and polycyclic groups, localization of nilpotent groups, commutator width and length, word maps and their images, and local word identities.

fields.title: Automorphisms of groups
fields.description: Automorphism and endomorphism groups of groups other than free groups: their orders and realizations, outer automorphism groups, class-preserving automorphisms, and automorphisms with few fixed points or twisted conjugacy classes.

subfields.title: Automorphism groups
subfields.description: The automorphism group as an object: orders of automorphism groups, realizing groups as (outer) automorphism groups, class-preserving and inner automorphisms, automorphism orbits, endomorphism counts.

subfields.title: Fixed points of automorphisms
subfields.description: How an automorphism and its fixed points control a group: almost regular and fixed-point-free automorphisms, bounds on derived length and Fitting height, twisted conjugacy, e- and nil-automorphisms, squares of 2-automorphisms.

fields.title: Periodic and locally finite groups
fields.description: Infinite groups defined by torsion and finiteness conditions: Burnside problems and free Burnside groups, Golod groups, Tarski monsters, locally finite simple groups, periodic Frobenius groups, minimal and weak chain conditions, and embeddings into simple periodic groups.

fields.title: Profinite and topological groups
fields.description: Groups with topology or approximated by finite quotients: profinite and pro-p groups, residual finiteness and separability, profinite rigidity, Golod–Shafarevich inequality, just-infinite groups, totally disconnected locally compact groups, group topologies, Lie groups and their dense subgroups.

fields.title: Linear groups
fields.description: Groups of matrices over fields and rings: SL2, PGL2 and SU(2) and their conjugacy and subgroups (Dickson's classification), Jordan, Malcev and Selberg theorems, transvections, eigenvalues of elements of prime order, and linearity of specific groups.

fields.title: Group rings
fields.description: Group rings and group algebras: unit and zero-divisor questions (Kaplansky unit conjecture), Zassenhaus conjectures, augmentation and dimension subgroups, Ore conditions, Jordan decomposition, projective modules over group rings.

fields.title: Combinatorics in groups
fields.description: Additive and Ramsey-type combinatorics inside groups: approximate subgroups and product theorems, small doubling, partitions and colourings of groups, dense and coset-free partitions, subset factorizations, products of large normal subsets.

fields.title: Group extensions and cohomology
fields.description: Extensions and complements (Schur–Zassenhaus), splitting of extensions, homology and first cohomology of groups, cohomological dimension, and integrability of groups as derived subgroups.

InformationTheory.title: Information Theory
InformationTheory.description: Information theory quantifies information, uncertainty, compression, and transmission through entropy and coding.

fields.title: Entropy and mutual information
fields.description: Shannon entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Kullback–Leibler divergence, the basic measures of uncertainty and dependence between random variables.

fields.title: Information inequalities
fields.description: Inequalities relating entropies, divergences and mutual information, such as the log-sum, Pinsker, Fano, data-processing and Shearer inequalities.

fields.title: Source coding
fields.description: Lossless compression of information sources by variable-length codes, including prefix codes, the Kraft–McMillan inequality and Shannon's source coding bounds.

fields.title: Channel simulation
fields.description: Simulating a noisy channel with shared randomness and auxiliary random variables, including one-shot channel simulation and the functional representation lemma.

fields.title: Error-correcting codes
fields.description: Codes that detect or correct transmission errors, including linear codes, Hamming and Reed–Solomon codes, cyclic redundancy checks, and the Hamming-space geometry used to bound them.

LinearAlgebra.title: Linear Algebra
LinearAlgebra.description: Linear algebra studies vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, duality, dimension, and spectral structure.

fields.title: Linear maps and duality
fields.description: Vector spaces and modules, linear maps and their invariants such as trace, dual spaces, dual bases and perfect pairings, and exactness of sequences of linear maps.

fields.title: Eigenvalues and canonical forms
fields.description: Eigenvalues, eigenspaces and characteristic polynomials of matrices and endomorphisms, and the normal forms they lead to: diagonalization, triangularization, Jordan and Smith normal forms.

fields.title: Matrix decompositions and linear systems
fields.description: Factorizations of matrices (singular value, polar, Schur and LU decompositions), Gaussian elimination and the solvability of linear systems, iterative methods and condition numbers.

fields.title: Determinants and matrix identities
fields.description: Determinant expansions and identities, determinants of special products and exponentials, derivatives of determinants, and algebraic identities between matrices.

fields.title: Positive definite matrices and matrix inequalities
fields.description: Positive definite and semidefinite matrices, criteria for definiteness, and inequalities for their determinants, traces and eigenvalues.

fields.title: Bilinear and quadratic forms
fields.description: Bilinear and quadratic forms on vector spaces and modules: rank, orthogonal sums, inertia and congruence, and lattices with their duals and neighbours.

fields.title: Special matrices
fields.description: Classes of matrices defined by their structure or entries: Toeplitz, Hankel and circulant matrices, Hadamard and sign matrices, combinatorial matrices, nonnegative, doubly stochastic and totally positive matrices.

Logic.title: Logic
Logic.description: Logic studies formal languages, proof, models, semantics, consistency, and the foundations of mathematical reasoning.

fields.title: Propositional logic and satisfiability
fields.description: Classical propositional logic: truth-table semantics, natural deduction and its completeness, functional completeness, normal forms and CNF transformations, resolution, interpolation, SAT-solving procedures (Davis–Putnam, DPLL, 2-SAT, Horn-SAT) and binary decision diagrams.

fields.title: First-order logic
fields.description: Syntax, proof calculi and semantics of first-order predicate logic, including soundness and Gödel's completeness theorem.

fields.title: Proof theory
fields.description: Structural study of formal proofs and provability: sequent calculi, linear logic and translations into it, and Gödel's incompleteness theorems.

fields.title: Modal logic
