fields.description: Logics of necessity and possibility interpreted on Kripke models, their axiomatizations, completeness and decidability, and extensions such as epistemic logic, dynamic logic and the modal μ-calculus.

fields.title: Temporal logic and model checking
fields.description: Linear and branching-time temporal logics interpreted over infinite words and transition systems, with automata-theoretic and fixed-point model-checking procedures.

fields.title: Model theory
fields.description: Relations between formal theories and their structures: first-order languages of algebraic structures, quantifier elimination, categoricity and o-minimality.

MeasureTheory.title: Measure Theory
MeasureTheory.description: Measure theory provides the language of size and integration underlying probability and modern analysis.

fields.title: Measures and measurable sets
fields.description: Construction and uniqueness of measures, atomless and vector measures, measures on Boolean algebras, and the limits of measurability shown by non-measurable sets and paradoxical decompositions.

fields.title: Lebesgue measure
fields.description: Lebesgue measure on the real line and Euclidean space: volumes of concrete bodies, null sets and density phenomena.

fields.title: Haar measure and fundamental domains
fields.description: Invariant measures on locally compact groups, unimodularity, and fundamental domains for the actions of discrete subgroups.

fields.title: Integration and convergence
fields.description: The Lebesgue integral and its convergence theorems, modes of convergence of measurable functions, approximation by simple functions, product measures, convolution, differentiation under the integral sign and integral inequalities.

fields.title: Lebesgue spaces
fields.description: The spaces Lp of p-th power integrable functions: membership criteria, inclusions, dense subspaces, the essential supremum and weak convergence.

fields.title: Differentiation of real functions
fields.description: Absolutely continuous, Lipschitz and bounded-variation functions of a real variable, maximal functions and almost-everywhere properties of real functions.

fields.title: Optimal transport
fields.description: Couplings of probability measures, transport costs and Kantorovich duality.

fields.title: Geometric measure theory
fields.description: Hausdorff measures and dimension, dimension functions and codimension, fractal sets such as attractors of iterated function systems, and the measure and dimension of distance sets.

NumberTheory.title: Number Theory
NumberTheory.description: Number theory studies integers, primes, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, and their analytic and algebraic structure.

fields.title: Congruences and power residues
fields.description: Modular arithmetic: Wilson, Wolstenholme and Fermat-quotient congruences, lifting the exponent, primitive roots, Legendre/Jacobi symbols, reciprocity, covering systems.

subfields.title: Congruences and modular arithmetic
subfields.description: Congruences for factorials, quotients and power sums (Wilson, Wolstenholme, Fermat quotients), lifting the exponent, multiplicative order, primitive roots, residue systems.

subfields.title: Power residues and reciprocity
subfields.description: Quadratic and cubic residues, Legendre, Jacobi and Kronecker symbols, quadratic reciprocity and its extensions, Legendre-symbol sums.

subfields.title: Covering systems
subfields.description: Covering and exact covering systems of residue classes, minimum moduli, Erdős–Graham and Fraenkel-type results.

fields.title: Primes and primality
fields.description: Individual primes and prime tests: special prime families, primality criteria, pseudoprimes, Carmichael numbers, Fermat and Mersenne numbers.

subfields.title: Primality tests and pseudoprimes
subfields.description: Primality criteria (Proth, Pocklington, Lucas–Lehmer), Fermat, Lucas, Frobenius and strong pseudoprimes, Carmichael and Korselt numbers.

subfields.title: Special classes of primes
subfields.description: Fermat, Mersenne, Sophie Germain, Wieferich, Cullen and other named prime families, Fermat numbers, Sierpiński–Riesel numbers, prime-producing formulas.

fields.title: Distribution of primes
fields.description: Counting primes: prime number theorem, explicit Chebyshev-type bounds, prime gaps and short intervals, primes in progressions, sieves, prime patterns.

subfields.title: Prime number theorem and explicit bounds
subfields.description: PNT and its proofs, Chebyshev theta and psi, explicit bounds for π(x) and the nth prime (Dusart, Axler, Rosser), Mertens constants.

subfields.title: Prime gaps and primes in short intervals
subfields.description: Bertrand-type and Breusch theorems, Ramanujan primes, prime gaps, bounded gaps, Sylvester–Schur on prime factors of consecutive products.

subfields.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions
subfields.description: Dirichlet density, PNT for progressions, Siegel–Walfisz, Bombieri–Vinogradov, Brun–Titchmarsh, prime races.

subfields.title: Sieve methods
subfields.description: Selberg, Brun and large sieves, almost primes, parity problem, counting integers with restricted prime factors via sieves.

subfields.title: Prime patterns and conjectures
subfields.description: Twin primes and Brun's constant, Hardy–Littlewood tuples, Goldbach/Lemoine-type statements, primes represented by polynomials (Friedlander–Iwaniec).

fields.title: Arithmetic functions
fields.description: Divisor sums, totients, Möbius and multiplicative functions, their mean values and extremal orders, and integers classified by them.

subfields.title: Perfect numbers and their relatives
subfields.description: Perfect, multiperfect, odd perfect, abundant, practical, Zumkeller, Giuga, amicable numbers, spoof factorizations, Lehmer's totient problem.

subfields.title: Divisor and totient functions
subfields.description: σ, τ, φ, Jordan and Dedekind ψ, unitary and biunitary divisors, gcd-sums, Ramanujan sums, totient multiplicities and values.

subfields.title: Multiplicative functions and mean values
subfields.description: Dirichlet and unitary convolution, completely multiplicative and additive functions, Wintner and Euler-product mean values, additive uniqueness sets, Mertens bounds.

subfields.title: Integers with restricted factorization
subfields.description: Squarefree, k-free, k-full and powerful, smooth and rough numbers, highly composite numbers, integers with prescribed prime factors.

fields.title: Zeta and L-functions
fields.description: Riemann zeta and xi, Dirichlet characters and L-functions, Dedekind and Artin L-functions, Riemann hypothesis criteria, multiple zeta values.

subfields.title: Riemann zeta function
subfields.description: Continuation and zeros of ζ, zero-free regions, moments and subconvexity, RH criteria (Robin, Lagarias), de Bruijn–Newman constant, zeta values.

subfields.title: Dirichlet characters and L-functions
subfields.description: Dirichlet characters, conductors, primitive and quadratic characters, Dirichlet series continuation, L-function bounds, Artin and Selberg-class functions.

subfields.title: Multiple zeta values
subfields.description: Multiple zeta and zeta-star values, Hoffman bases, word algebras, cyclic sum formulas, finite and q-analogue multiple zeta values.

fields.title: Exponential and character sums
fields.description: Gauss sums, Weyl and Vinogradov sums, incomplete exponential sums, Burgess bounds, Dirichlet polynomials, trigonometric and cotangent sums.

fields.title: Diophantine equations
fields.description: Integer and rational solutions of polynomial and exponential equations, Pell equations, Thue equations, Diophantine tuples, Egyptian fractions.

subfields.title: Exponential Diophantine equations
subfields.description: Equations with unknown exponents: Pillai, Catalan, Størmer, Nagell–Ljunggren, Ramanujan–Nagell and Terai-type equations, powers plus one.

subfields.title: Pell and quadratic Diophantine equations
subfields.description: Pell and negative Pell equations, norm equations, Pythagorean triples, Markov triples and quadratic equations in two or three variables.

subfields.title: Higher-degree Diophantine equations
subfields.description: Thue equations, generalized Fermat equations, sums of cubes, x^y = y^x, abc conjecture, Brocard–Ramanujan and symmetric-function equations.

subfields.title: Diophantine tuples and Egyptian fractions
subfields.description: Diophantine m-tuples, Erdős–Straus problem, Egyptian fraction representations and greedy unit-fraction algorithms.

fields.title: Quadratic forms and sums of squares
fields.description: Representations by quadratic forms: sums of two, three and four squares, binary forms and class numbers, universality theorems, Waring's problem.

subfields.title: Sums of squares and representation numbers
subfields.description: Two-, three- and four-square theorems, Jacobi-type counts, Gaussian and Hurwitz integer methods, x²+2y² and similar representations.

subfields.title: Binary and higher quadratic forms
subfields.description: Reduction theory, discriminants and class numbers of binary forms, quaternary forms, 15 and 290 theorems.

subfields.title: Waring's problem and figurate numbers
subfields.description: Hilbert–Waring, g(3)=9, Fermat polygonal theorem, polygonal, triangular and polytopic numbers and their sums.

fields.title: Diophantine approximation and transcendence
fields.description: Approximating reals by rationals or algebraics, Roth and subspace theorems, linear forms in logarithms, transcendence, uniform distribution, geometry of numbers.

subfields.title: Transcendence and irrationality
subfields.description: Hermite–Lindemann, Lindemann–Weierstrass, Gelfond–Schneider, Mahler functions, irrationality and linear independence of constants.

subfields.title: Roth's theorem and linear forms in logarithms
subfields.description: Thue–Siegel–Roth, Ridout, Schmidt subspace, Baker, Baker–Wüstholz, Matveev bounds, Baker–Davenport reduction, approximation by algebraic numbers.

subfields.title: Uniform distribution and metric approximation
subfields.description: Weyl equidistribution, three-gap theorem, Duffin–Schaeffer, normal numbers, Beatty sequences, discrepancy, lattice points and Minkowski-type theorems.

fields.title: Continued fractions and expansions of reals
fields.description: Continued fractions, Farey sequences, Stern–Brocot tree, Engel, Pierce, Lüroth and similar series expansions of real numbers.

fields.title: Heights and Mahler measure
fields.description: Absolute heights of algebraic numbers, Mahler measure, Lehmer's problem, Dobrowolski bounds, Schinzel–Zassenhaus, house and trace problems.

fields.title: Algebraic number theory
fields.description: Number fields and rings of integers: quadratic and cyclotomic fields, discriminants, ramification, ideals, adeles and ideles, class field theory.

subfields.title: Quadratic fields and integer rings
subfields.description: Gaussian, Eisenstein and ℤ[√d] integers, prime factorization there, imaginary quadratic discriminants, class numbers, Stark–Heegner.

subfields.title: Cyclotomic fields
subfields.description: Cyclotomic fields and polynomials, real cyclotomic polynomials, 2cos(2πk/n), cyclotomic units, ramification and inertness in cyclotomic fields.

subfields.title: Discriminants, ramification and ideals
subfields.description: Discriminants and their bounds, ramification and inertia, orders, units, ideal counting, local degrees under completion, field enumeration and towers.

subfields.title: Adeles, ideles and class field theory
subfields.description: Places, adeles and ideles, Arakelov divisors, ray class groups, Artin map, Hilbert class fields, Neukirch–Uchida-type Galois characterization.

fields.title: p-adic numbers and local fields
fields.description: p-adic integers and expansions, valuations of integer sequences, Hensel lifting, Strassmann's theorem, Hilbert symbols, p-adic gamma, local fields.

fields.title: Modular forms, q-series and partitions
fields.description: Modular forms and functions, congruence subgroups, Ramanujan tau, theta functions, mock theta functions, Lambert series, partition congruences.

subfields.title: Modular forms
subfields.description: Modular and cusp forms, congruence subgroups, cusps, Eisenstein series congruences, Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture, spectral gaps.

subfields.title: Theta functions and q-series
subfields.description: Jacobi and Ramanujan theta functions, q-Pochhammer symbols and Euler products, Rogers–Ramanujan and related continued fractions, mock theta functions, Lambert series and q-series identities.

subfields.title: Partition congruences
subfields.description: Ramanujan-type congruences, dissections and densities for partition functions and their variants (overpartitions, regular, cubic, core, colored, mex, designated-summand and smallest-part partitions), proved with q-series and eta quotients.

fields.title: Linear recurrence sequences
fields.description: Fibonacci, Lucas, Pell, Tribonacci and other linear recurrences: identities, divisibility, periods, primitive divisors and Diophantine properties.

subfields.title: Fibonacci and Lucas numbers
subfields.description: Identities, sums, reciprocal series, determinants and generating functions specifically for Fibonacci and Lucas numbers.

subfields.title: Lucas sequences and primitive divisors
subfields.description: General Lucas sequences U_n, V_n, Lucas pairs, divisibility, Bang–Zsigmondy and primitive-divisor theorems, Fibonacci prime divisibility.

subfields.title: Pell, Jacobsthal and other second-order sequences
subfields.description: Pell, Pell–Lucas, Jacobsthal, gibonacci, Horadam, Leonardo, Oresme, bi-periodic and (a,b)-Fibonacci sequences.

subfields.title: Tribonacci and higher-order sequences
subfields.description: Tribonacci, tetranacci, pentanacci, k-generalized Fibonacci, Padovan, Perrin and Narayana sequences, dominant roots and Binet forms.

subfields.title: Fibonacci and Lucas polynomials
subfields.description: Fibonacci, Lucas, Jacobsthal and gibonacci polynomials, their sums, squares and generating function values.

subfields.title: General theory of recurrences
subfields.description: C-finite, P-recursive and MC-finite sequences, Binet formulas, Skolem–Mahler–Lech, growth, generating functions and decomposable forms.

subfields.title: Recurrences modulo m
subfields.description: Pisano periods, periods and zero indices of recurrences modulo primes and prime powers, residue distribution.

subfields.title: Diophantine problems in recurrences
subfields.description: Squares, perfect powers, repdigits, factorials and powers of two among terms of recurrence sequences.

fields.title: Special numbers and polynomials
fields.description: Arithmetic of classical number families: Bernoulli, Euler and Genocchi numbers, harmonic numbers, binomial and Catalan-type coefficients.

subfields.title: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials
subfields.description: Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, identities, denominators, Kummer congruences, Faulhaber sums, Appell sequences, higher-order and Apostol variants.

subfields.title: Euler, Genocchi and poly-Bernoulli numbers
subfields.description: Euler numbers and polynomials, Genocchi numbers, poly-Bernoulli, Bernoulli of the second kind, degenerate variants.

subfields.title: Harmonic numbers and harmonic sums
subfields.description: Harmonic, hyperharmonic and multiple harmonic sums, binomial-harmonic identities, non-integrality, harmonic congruences, Euler–Mascheroni bounds.

subfields.title: Binomial coefficients and factorials
subfields.description: Divisibility and valuations of binomial coefficients, Lucas-type theorems, factorial ratios and Fibonomial coefficients; b-nomial, totienomial and other generalized binomial coefficients go to Combinatorics.

subfields.title: Catalan and Fuss–Catalan numbers
subfields.description: Catalan, Fuss–Catalan, Lucasnomial and FiboCatalan numbers: integrality and prime divisibility.

fields.title: Digits and numeration systems
fields.description: Base-b digits of integers, repdigits and palindromes, Kaprekar and happy numbers, Zeckendorf and base-φ systems, automatic sequences.

subfields.title: Digit properties of integers
subfields.description: Digit sums and products, Niven, happy, Kaprekar, Keith numbers, comma sequences, decimal expansions of fractions (Midy, repetends).

subfields.title: Repdigits, palindromes and reverse multiples
subfields.description: Repdigits, palindromes, reverse multiples and Young graphs, permutiples, digit reversal, special squares by digits.

subfields.title: Numeration systems and automatic sequences
subfields.description: Zeckendorf, base-φ, negative and signed bases, Cobham's theorem, base-recognizable sets, Mahler substitution, regular sequences.

fields.title: Integer sequences
fields.description: Named nonlinear integer sequences: Collatz and iterated maps, self-referential sequences, Sylvester and Euclid sequences, realizable and Dold sequences.

subfields.title: Iterated maps and self-referential sequences
subfields.description: Collatz problem, EKG, Stern diatomic, Hofstadter, Golomb, Ulam, Ducci, Josephus and Conway-type sequences.

subfields.title: Arithmetic properties of sequences
subfields.description: Dold, Newton and realizable sequences, Sylvester, Euclid and Göbel sequences, gcd and divisibility sequences, OEIS-specific sequences.

fields.title: Additive number theory
fields.description: Representing integers as sums from special sets, and the density of integer sets: sumsets of integers, subset sums and complete sequences, primitive sets, natural and logarithmic density, Romanoff's theorem; additive bases and complements and zero-sum constants go to additive combinatorics.

fields.title: Numerical semigroups and the Frobenius problem
fields.description: Sylvester's coin theorem, Frobenius numbers, pseudo-Frobenius sets and numerical semigroups generated by special sequences.

fields.title: Arithmetic geometry
fields.description: Rational points of varieties over number fields: torsion and rank of elliptic curves, naive heights, Hasse principle, local-global failures.

fields.title: Arithmetic of function fields
fields.description: Number-theoretic analogues over F_q[T] and finite fields: polynomial primes, h-free polynomials, function-field adeles, positive-characteristic zeta values.

Order.title: Order Theory
Order.description: Order theory studies comparison relations, lattices, intervals, monotonicity, and order-complete constructions.

fields.title: Ordered sets
fields.description: Partial, strict and total orders, dense linear orders, monotone maps and sequences, and representations of finite posets.

fields.title: Lattices and Boolean algebras
fields.description: Lattices and Boolean algebras, their representation theorems, and Boolean functions viewed as maps between Boolean lattices.

fields.title: Fixed points and domain theory
fields.description: Least and greatest fixed points of monotone and Scott-continuous maps, Kleene iteration, and the complete partial orders that underlie denotational semantics.

Probability.title: Probability
Probability.description: Probability studies random phenomena through distributions, expectation, independence, concentration, and stochastic processes.

fields.title: Foundations of probability
fields.description: Construction of probability measures and processes (Kolmogorov extension, measures from Stieltjes functions), independence, conditional expectation and regular conditional distributions, exchangeability and de Finetti's theorem, and zero–one laws for sequences (Hewitt–Savage); zero–one laws for continuous processes go to Brownian motion and stochastic calculus, tail sigma-algebras of random walks to Random walks.

fields.title: Probability distributions
fields.description: Named discrete and continuous laws and their moments, densities, mass functions and tails (binomial, Poisson-binomial, hypergeometric, negative binomial, beta, gamma, exponential, chi-square, Dirichlet, multivariate Gaussian and Gaussian conditioning, Gaussian orthant probabilities), expectation under a probability mass function, joint laws, distribution functions, quantiles and medians; sampling laws used in tests (t, F) go to Linear models and multivariate analysis.

fields.title: Characteristic functions and generating functions
fields.description: Characteristic functions, probability generating functions and positive-definite functions (Bochner), Taylor bounds for characteristic functions, lattice support, Lévy's continuity theorem and Cramér's decomposition theorem for the normal law.

fields.title: Infinitely divisible laws and regular variation
fields.description: Infinitely divisible and stable distributions, convolution powers, the Lévy–Khintchin representation, and regularly varying and slowly varying functions (Karamata's theorem, Potter bounds, generalized inverses) with the truncated moments and tail integrals of heavy-tailed laws.

fields.title: Convergence of probability measures
fields.description: Weak convergence and convergence in probability, tightness and Prokhorov's theorem, Helly selection, Skorokhod representation, the continuous mapping theorem, the Cramér–Wold device and total variation distance; specific limit laws go to the limit-theorem fields.

fields.title: Laws of large numbers and random series
fields.description: Almost-sure behaviour of sums of independent variables: strong and weak laws of large numbers, Kolmogorov's three-series theorem and maximal inequality, truncation techniques, the law of the iterated logarithm, and the Monte Carlo variance rate of sample means.

fields.title: Central limit theorems and Poisson approximation
fields.description: Convergence in law of normalized sums and their error terms: central limit theorems (Lindeberg–Feller, lacunary and infinite-variance variants), Berry–Esseen bounds and constants, global and local de Moivre–Laplace theorems, Edgeworth expansions, Donsker's invariance principle, and Poisson limit theorems for binomial and urn models.

fields.title: Large deviations
fields.description: Large deviation principles and rate functions, Cramér's theorem and Chernoff bounds for empirical means, log-moment generating functions and the Legendre–Fenchel transform used to build them.

fields.title: Concentration inequalities
fields.description: Non-asymptotic tail and moment bounds: Hoeffding, McDiarmid, Efron–Stein, Khintchine and Paley–Zygmund inequalities, sampling without replacement, sub-Gaussian convex comparison, and hypercontractivity (Bonami–Beckner, p-biased two-point inequalities) on the discrete cube.

fields.title: Martingales and optional stopping
fields.description: Discrete-time martingales, sub- and supermartingales: convergence theorems (almost sure, L^p, backwards, Lévy's downward theorem), uniform integrability, Doob's maximal inequalities, orthogonality and conditional variance of increments, optional stopping in all its forms, and Wald's equations for stopped sums. Martingale measures and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing.

fields.title: Random walks
fields.description: Sums of i.i.d. steps as processes: the drift/oscillation dichotomy, limsup and liminf of partial sums, tail measurability of asymptotic events, the strong Markov property of i.i.d. sequences at stopping times, and ballot theorems.

fields.title: Markov chains
fields.description: Discrete-time Markov chains (construction, path measures, finite-dimensional distributions, Chapman–Kolmogorov, Markov and strong Markov properties), finite chains, ergodicity and convergence to stationarity, mixing, reversibility and Kolmogorov's cycle criterion, and finite continuous-time Markov chains with rate matrices, semigroups and hitting times.

fields.title: Branching processes
fields.description: Galton–Watson processes, extinction probabilities, total progeny and the hitting-time theorem, and linear birth–death processes.

fields.title: Brownian motion and stochastic calculus
fields.description: Continuous-time processes with continuous paths or independent increments: Kolmogorov's continuity theorem, Blumenthal-type zero–one laws, Markov property for independent-increment processes, quadratic variation, the Itô integral and Itô's formula, stochastic differential equations, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, and Fokker–Planck equations for diffusions.

fields.title: Point processes and stationary processes
fields.description: Poisson processes on the line and Poisson point processes on general spaces (arrival times, counts, restriction theorem), and stationary random functions.

fields.title: Random fields on lattices
fields.description: Spin and bond configuration spaces, Bernoulli product measures and cylinder events, Gibbs-type conditional distributions given the outside of a region, translation invariance and ergodicity, weak and monotone limits of measures on configuration space, and marginals and conditional independence for weights on finite configuration spaces.

fields.title: Percolation
fields.description: Bernoulli bond and site percolation: percolation probability, critical points, number and uniqueness of infinite clusters, sharpness and sharp thresholds, and crossing estimates in two dimensions.

subfields.title: Phase transition and critical probability
subfields.description: The percolation probability theta, bounds 0 < p_c < 1 (Peierls and enclosure arguments), percolation on product graphs, the number and uniqueness of infinite clusters (Burton–Keane), and sharp thresholds from influences (KKL).

subfields.title: Sharpness of the phase transition
subfields.description: The Duminil-Copin–Tassion proof of exponential decay below p_c: the quantity phi_p(S), Russo's formula and pivotal edges, exploration and last-exit decompositions, the differential inequality, the mean-field bound and subcritical decay.

subfields.title: Crossing probabilities in two dimensions
subfields.description: Crossings of rectangles and annuli in bond percolation on Z^2, the box-crossing property, gluing and square-root tricks, Russo–Seymour–Welsh theory and planar separation lemmas.

fields.title: Correlation inequalities and stochastic domination
fields.description: Inequalities comparing probabilities of monotone or disjointly occurring events under product measures, and stochastic orderings and monotone couplings of measures.

subfields.title: Harris, FKG and BK inequalities
subfields.description: Increasing events, the Harris and FKG inequalities, Holley's inequality, disjoint occurrence and the van den Berg–Kesten inequality (finite, countable and inhomogeneous), pivotal coordinates and Russo's formula on product spaces.

subfields.title: Reimer's inequality
subfields.description: Reimer's inequality for arbitrary events and its proof machinery: configurations as finsets, down-compression, doubled ground sets, disjoint-pair counts and weighted pair sums, and special and mixed-monotone cases.

fields.title: High-dimensional and geometric probability
fields.description: Probability in high dimension and on geometric objects: log-concave and uniform convex-body laws, isotropic constants, the KLS and thin-shell conjectures and their bounds, random matrices (singularity of Bernoulli matrices, Tracy–Widom limits), and random Euclidean optimization (Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley).

fields.title: Statistical estimation
fields.description: Point estimation theory: bias, risk and mean squared error, likelihood and maximum likelihood (consistency and asymptotic normality), Fisher information and Cramér–Rao, sufficiency, factorization (Fisher–Neyman, Halmos–Savage) and Rao–Blackwell, Stein's lemma and James–Stein shrinkage, and contiguity and local asymptotic normality.

fields.title: Hypothesis testing
fields.description: Tests and their validity and power: Neyman–Pearson, likelihood-ratio, score and Wald tests, monotone likelihood ratio, exact conditional tests (Fisher, Hardy–Weinberg), rank tests and ROC area (Mann–Whitney), permutation p-values, multiple testing (Bonferroni, Holm, closed testing, Benjamini–Hochberg, false discovery rates), and meta-analysis and heterogeneity statistics.

fields.title: Linear models and multivariate analysis
fields.description: Multivariate normal theory and linear models: Gaussian maximum likelihood, Cochran's theorem on quadratic forms, t and F sampling laws, Gauss–Markov and generalized least squares, principal component analysis, and Gaussian graphical models.

fields.title: Nonparametric statistics and survival analysis
fields.description: Distribution-free and semiparametric methods: empirical distribution functions (Glivenko–Cantelli), U-statistics, the Kaplan–Meier estimator, Cox partial likelihood and the log-rank test, and design-based causal inference with potential outcomes.

fields.title: Bayesian statistics
fields.description: Bayesian inference and nonparametric priors: the Dirichlet process and stick-breaking, Pólya and Blackwell–MacQueen urns, Ferguson conjugacy, and posterior computations.

QuantumInformation.title: Quantum Information
QuantumInformation.description: Quantum information studies states, channels, measurement, entanglement, communication, and quantum computation.

fields.title: Quantum foundations
fields.description: Quantum foundations studies what quantum mechanics rules out and allows at the level of measurement outcomes, including contextuality, Bell nonlocality and bounds on quantum correlations.

fields.title: Quantum operations and channels
fields.description: Quantum operations and channels covers the physically allowed transformations of quantum states, such as isometries and completely positive maps, and impossibility results like the no-cloning theorem.

RepresentationTheory.title: Representation Theory
RepresentationTheory.description: Representation theory studies symmetry by realizing groups and algebras as transformations of linear spaces.

fields.title: Representations of finite groups
fields.description: Ordinary representation theory of finite groups over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero: characters, irreducibility, Schur's lemma, multiplicities and the Wedderburn decomposition of the group algebra.

fields.title: Group cohomology
fields.description: Homology, cohomology and Tate cohomology of groups with coefficients in modules, with their functoriality, additivity, periodicity and the Herbrand quotient.

fields.title: Representations of topological and Lie groups
fields.description: Representations of infinite groups and Lie algebras: continuous and unitary representations of compact and topological groups (Peter–Weyl theorem, complete reducibility), continuous representations over topological rings, representations of Lie algebras and of general linear groups (Schur–Weyl duality), and groups characterized by their irreducible representations.

RingTheory.title: Ring Theory
RingTheory.description: Ring theory studies addition and multiplication through ideals, modules, localization, dimension, and homological structure.

fields.title: Dedekind domains and ideal theory
fields.description: Dedekind domains and their characterizations, unique factorization of fractional ideals into primes, the ideal class group, invertible fractional ideals and the conductor of an order.

fields.title: Ramification theory
fields.description: How primes split, ramify and stay inert in finite extensions of Dedekind domains and discrete valuation rings, measured by the different, the discriminant, ramification indices, inertia degrees and Frobenius elements.

fields.title: Valuation rings and Henselian rings
fields.description: Discrete valuation rings and general valuation rings, their completions and finite extensions, residue fields, Hensel's lemma and the Krull–Akizuki theorem.

fields.title: Local rings, dimension and completion
fields.description: Local rings and their residue fields, Krull dimension, adic completion, regular local rings and length of modules.

fields.title: Ideals, localization and ring constructions
fields.description: Ideals and submodules under localization, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, zero divisors, products of rings and fields, and ring constructions such as Witt vectors.

fields.title: Étale algebras, norms and differentials
fields.description: Algebras over commutative rings: étale algebras and the trace form, norm and trace maps, Kähler differentials and derivations.

fields.title: Syzygies and free resolutions
fields.description: Free resolutions of modules over polynomial rings, Hilbert's syzygy theorem, and graded Betti numbers and Poincaré series of multigraded modules.

fields.title: Formal power series
fields.description: Rings of formal power series in one or several variables and Hahn series, with formal exponentials, derivatives, coefficient operators and Lagrange inversion.

fields.title: Modules over commutative rings
fields.description: Projective, free and finitely generated modules over commutative rings and module-finite extensions: Kaplansky's theorem, the Quillen–Suslin theorem, descent of Noetherianness (Eakin–Nagata) and the direct summand theorem.

fields.title: Invariant theory
fields.description: Rings of invariants of finite groups acting on commutative rings: finiteness of invariant rings and Hilbert–Poincaré series of modular invariant rings of polynomial algebras.

SetTheory.title: Set Theory
SetTheory.description: Set theory studies membership, cardinality, ordinals, infinity, and foundational constructions for mathematics.

fields.title: Cardinal arithmetic and cardinal characteristics
fields.description: The arithmetic of infinite cardinals, including the continuum hypothesis and the singular cardinals hypothesis, together with cardinal invariants of the continuum and the cofinal structure of directed sets.

fields.title: Large cardinals
fields.description: Cardinals with strong closure or reflection properties, such as inaccessible, Mahlo, weakly compact and measurable cardinals, whose existence cannot be proved in ZFC.

fields.title: Infinitary combinatorics
fields.description: Combinatorics of infinite and uncountable sets: clubs and stationary sets, partition relations, Δ-systems, almost disjoint families, combinatorial principles such as diamond and square, set-theoretic trees, Ramsey ultrafilters and the structure of P(ω)/fin.

fields.title: Forcing and forcing axioms
fields.description: The forcing method and the axioms that assert the existence of generic filters, such as Martin's axiom and the proper forcing axiom, together with combinatorial dichotomies like the open coloring axiom and the P-ideal dichotomy that follow from them.

StatisticalMechanics.title: Statistical Mechanics
StatisticalMechanics.description: Statistical mechanics studies lattice models of interacting spins and bonds through Gibbs measures, partition functions, correlation inequalities, and phase transitions.

fields.title: Lattice spin models
fields.description: Spin models on finite graphs: the Ising Hamiltonian, Gibbs distribution and partition function and their agreement with the canonical ensemble, the pressure and its independence of boundary conditions, and the Lee–Yang theorem on the zeros of the partition function.

fields.title: Correlation inequalities for spin systems
fields.description: Inequalities for the correlations of ferromagnetic Ising models: the Griffiths (GKS) and FKG inequalities, monotonicity in the couplings and the temperature, and the Griffiths–Hurst–Sherman inequality with its consequences for the magnetization.

fields.title: Gibbs states and phase transitions
fields.description: Infinite-volume states of the Ising model and its phase transition: weak limits of box measures and the DLR condition, translation invariance, ergodicity and extremality of the plus state, spontaneous magnetization and the critical temperature, and Peierls' contour argument for long-range order.

fields.title: Exact solutions and duality
fields.description: Exact results for the two-dimensional Ising model: Kramers–Wannier duality between high- and low-temperature expansions, and Onsager's formula for the free energy through Kac–Ward determinants, Sherman's loop identities and the homology of the torus.

fields.title: Random currents and sharpness
fields.description: The random-current representation of Ising correlations and the switching lemma, and the sharpness of the Ising phase transition: the Simon–Lieb inequality, exponential decay of correlations below the critical point and the mean-field lower bound on the magnetization above it.

fields.title: Random-cluster model
fields.description: The random-cluster (Fortuin–Kasteleyn) model and its Edwards–Sokal coupling with the Potts and Ising models: finite-volume measures, the FKG inequality and comparison with Bernoulli percolation, infinite-volume limits, translation invariance and ergodicity, the free energy, agreement of free and wired measures, and the critical point.

TheoryOfComputation.title: Theory of Computation
TheoryOfComputation.description: The mathematical study of what can be computed and at what cost: machine models, computability and undecidability, automata and formal languages, and computational complexity.

fields.title: Turing machines
fields.description: Definitions, semantics and programming of Turing machines (single-tape, multi-tape and multi-stack), simulations between tape models, and universal machines with their machine codes. Results showing that a model computes exactly the recursive functions go to Equivalence of models of computation.

subfields.title: Single-tape Turing machines
subfields.description: Single-tape machines: configurations, steps, halting, composition of machines, tape views, state restriction, and translation of multi-stack machines to one tape (simulation and its halting behaviour, not its time cost).

subfields.title: Multi-tape and multi-stack machines
subfields.description: Multi-tape and multi-stack (TM2) machines and their program library: bit primitives, cleanup, composition, stack embeddings and generic host machines that run component machines, and state relabelling.

subfields.title: Universal Turing machines
subfields.description: Codes for machines, clocked evaluators and universal machines, completeness of codes, and the cost of universal simulation. Diagonalization against time-bounded codes goes to Hierarchy theorems.

fields.title: Equivalence of models of computation
fields.description: Register (URM), counter and RAM machines, and theorems that Turing machines and other models compute exactly the partial recursive functions or decide and recognize exactly the recursive and r.e. predicates (Church–Turing equivalences).

fields.title: Computability and undecidability
fields.description: Recursive and recursively enumerable predicates and their closure properties, the halting problem, Rice's and Rice–Shapiro theorems, the recursion and s-m-n theorems, enumerators, index sets such as totality, finiteness and minimal programs, and Busy Beaver functions.

fields.title: Degrees of unsolvability and the arithmetical hierarchy
fields.description: Turing and many-one reducibility, Turing degrees and the jump, recursive isomorphism (Myhill), productive, creative, simple and immune sets, r.e.-completeness, and the arithmetical hierarchy.

fields.title: Undecidable problems
fields.description: Specific undecidable problems and the reductions proving them undecidable: the Post correspondence problem and its variants, string rewriting, undecidable questions about context-free grammars (ambiguity, intersection, universality, regularity), and emptiness of linear bounded automata.

fields.title: Decision procedures for automata, grammars and strings
fields.description: Algorithms deciding questions about finite automata, regular expressions and context-free grammars given as data: emptiness, membership, universality, equivalence, and computable grammar reduction, together with the encodings of automata and grammars they operate on; and satisfiability of string constraints (word equations with regular membership and length bounds).

fields.title: Finite automata and regular languages
fields.description: Deterministic, nondeterministic, two-way and ε-automata, transducers, regular expressions and Kleene's theorem, closure properties of regular languages, automaton minimization, and the algebraic theory of recognition by monoids.

subfields.title: Automata and regular expressions
subfields.description: DFA, NFA, ε-NFA and two-way automata, sequential transducers and Mealy and Moore machines, regular expressions, Thompson's construction and Kleene's theorem, star height, and closure of regular languages under homomorphism, quotient, shuffle and substitution.

subfields.title: Automaton minimization
subfields.description: Nerode equivalence, the minimal automaton and its universal property, and the minimization algorithms of Moore, Hopcroft and Brzozowski with their correctness and cost.

subfields.title: Syntactic monoids and algebraic recognition
subfields.description: Recognition of languages by monoid morphisms, syntactic congruences and monoids, transition monoids, language contexts and quotients, and inverse images under word morphisms.

fields.title: Automata on infinite words and infinite games
fields.description: Büchi, generalized Büchi, parity, Rabin, Streett and Muller automata on infinite words, their emptiness and conversions, and parity games with attractors and traps.

fields.title: Context-free languages
fields.description: Context-free grammars and derivations, normal forms, parsing algorithms, pushdown automata, deterministic and ambiguous languages, closure and non-closure properties, pumping and Ogden's lemmas, and Parikh images.

subfields.title: Grammars, parsing and pushdown automata
subfields.description: Grammar basics and derivation forests, Chomsky and Greibach normal forms, ε- and unit-production elimination, CYK and Earley recognizers, leftmost derivations and (inherent) ambiguity, pushdown automata, deterministic context-free languages, and the grammar–PDA equivalence.

subfields.title: Closure properties and pumping lemmas
subfields.description: Closure of context-free languages under union, concatenation, star, homomorphism, inverse homomorphism, substitution, regular intersection and quotients, non-closure under intersection and complement, the pumping and Ogden lemmas, and Parikh's theorem.

fields.title: Context-sensitive languages
fields.description: Context-sensitive grammars, linear bounded automata and space-bounded single-tape machines, and the equivalence between them.

fields.title: Complexity classes
fields.description: Definitions of time and space complexity on machine models (P, NP, PSPACE, EXP, L, NL, the polynomial hierarchy, FPT and W[1]), polynomial-time encodings and reductions, simulation overheads, Blum measures, and inclusions and collapses among deterministic and nondeterministic classes (Savitch, Immerman–Szelepcsényi, Karp–Lipton, Ladner, Mahaney). Randomized, counting, circuit and quantum classes have their own fields.

fields.title: Hierarchy theorems and proof barriers
fields.description: Time and space hierarchy theorems and diagonalization against time-bounded machines, separations such as P ≠ EXP, and barriers to separating classes: relativization (Baker–Gill–Solovay, oracle separations), natural proofs and algebrization.

fields.title: Randomized, interactive and quantum complexity
fields.description: Probabilistic classes (RP, BPP), Arthur–Merlin and interactive proofs (AM, MA, IP = PSPACE, graph (non)isomorphism), BPP versus nonuniform and alternating classes, randomized reductions (Valiant–Vazirani), and quantum classes BQP and QMA.

fields.title: Counting complexity
fields.description: #P and PP: #P-completeness (counting SAT, permanent), PP-completeness, Toda's theorem, threshold languages, and approximate counting algorithms and schemes (Stockmeyer, Karp–Luby, Jerrum–Sinclair–Vigoda).

fields.title: Pseudorandomness and one-way functions
fields.description: Complexity-theoretic foundations of cryptography and derandomization: one-way functions, hardcore predicates (Goldreich–Levin), hardness amplification (Yao's XOR lemma), hardness-versus-randomness generators (Nisan–Wigderson), and Impagliazzo's five worlds.

fields.title: Boolean circuit complexity
fields.description: Boolean circuits as a model of computation, including arithmetic circuits built from gates (adders, two's complement), parallel classes AC0, NC1 and NC, and circuit lower bounds (parity and majority not in AC0, Smolensky, Razborov's monotone bound, Shannon counting, Williams).

fields.title: Algebraic complexity
fields.description: Arithmetic circuits over a field and the complexity of algebraic problems: matrix multiplication exponents (square, rectangular, dual) and their bounds, tensor rank, and the bit complexity of integer multiplication.

fields.title: Descriptive complexity
fields.description: Logical characterizations of complexity classes on finite structures: Fagin's theorem, Immerman–Vardi (least fixed point and P), and transitive closure logic and NL.

fields.title: Kolmogorov complexity
fields.description: Algorithmic information content of individual strings: universal description methods, incompressible strings, non-computability and upper semicomputability of Kolmogorov complexity.

fields.title: NP-completeness
fields.description: The Cook–Levin theorem and NP-completeness of specific decision problems, by the problem's domain; includes both machine-level Karp reductions and stated NP-completeness results.

subfields.title: Cook–Levin theorem
subfields.description: The Cook–Levin theorem and its machinery: SAT verifiers, dense and binary CNF encodings and converters between them, tableau formulas and the generator machines that emit them.

subfields.title: Satisfiability and constraint satisfaction
subfields.description: Variants of SAT and CSP: 3SAT and the SAT-to-3SAT reduction, bounded-occurrence, monotone, not-all-equal and 1-in-3 SAT, MAX-SAT, MAX-2SAT, MIN-ONES, circuit SAT, binary CSP and betweenness.

subfields.title: Cliques, covers and domination in graphs
subfields.description: Clique, independent set, vertex cover, domination variants, feedback vertex and arc sets, odd cycle transversal, bicliques, densest subgraph, induced matching and minimum fill-in.

subfields.title: Graph coloring, cuts and layouts
subfields.description: Vertex, edge, list and precoloring-extension coloring, achromatic number, graph homomorphism, maximum and k-cuts, bisection, multiway cut, partition into triangles or paths, bandwidth, linear arrangement and linear ordering.

subfields.title: Paths, cycles, trees and subgraph problems
subfields.description: Hamiltonian paths and cycles, longest paths and cycles, disjoint paths and path covers, constrained spanning and Steiner trees, minimum equivalent digraph, traveling salesperson and vehicle routing, and (induced) subgraph isomorphism.

subfields.title: Number partitioning, knapsack and packing
subfields.description: Subset sum, subset product, partition, 3-partition, multiway partition, knapsack variants, bin and strip packing, numerical 3-dimensional matching and 0-1 integer programming.

subfields.title: Set systems, assignment and location
subfields.description: 3-dimensional matching, exact cover, set cover, set packing, set splitting, maximum coverage, minimum test set, generalized and quadratic assignment, facility location, k-center and k-median.

subfields.title: Scheduling problems
subfields.description: Single-machine, parallel-machine, flow-shop, precedence-constrained and resource-constrained scheduling with deadlines, tardiness or weighted completion objectives.

subfields.title: Strings, puzzles and Latin squares
subfields.description: String problems (closest string, longest common subsequence, shortest common supersequence) and puzzles (Sudoku, Nonogram, Akari, Minesweeper, Latin square completion).

fields.title: Probabilistically checkable proofs and inapproximability
fields.description: The PCP theorem and Dinur's gap amplification, optimization classes (NPO, APX, MAXSNP), and hardness of approximation results such as Håstad's MAX-3SAT bound and the absence of a PTAS for MAX-CUT.

fields.title: Completeness for other complexity classes
fields.description: Problems complete for classes other than NP: P (circuit value), NL (s-t connectivity), coNP (UNSAT), PSPACE (TQBF, Geography), levels of the polynomial hierarchy (QSAT_k), EXP, NEXP and EXPSPACE (succinct problems, regular expressions with squaring).

fields.title: Problems solvable in polynomial time
fields.description: Proofs or statements that specific problems lie in P or L: graph reachability (PATH) with its marking machine, undirected connectivity in L, 2-SAT, primality, matching, maximum flow, linear programming, integer programming in fixed dimension, and hypergraph matching and cut questions.

fields.title: Fine-grained and exponential-time complexity
fields.description: Exact running times of hard problems beyond the polynomial/non-polynomial divide: exponential, subexponential and quasipolynomial algorithms for NP-hard or NP-intermediate problems, such as the tensor-network 2^o(n)-time algorithm for 3-SAT and Babai's quasipolynomial-time graph isomorphism theorem, and the exponential time hypothesis.

Topology.title: Topology
Topology.description: Topology studies continuity, open sets, compactness, connectedness, and invariants preserved by homeomorphism.

fields.title: General topology
fields.description: Point-set topology of topological and metric spaces: connectedness, separation and cardinal invariants, homogeneous spaces, direct and inverse limits of spaces, restricted products, and dimension theory.

fields.title: Descriptive set theory
fields.description: The topology of Polish spaces and their definable subsets: classical characterizations of Cantor space, Baire space and the rationals, Borel complexity, Bernstein sets and topological games.

fields.title: Continuum theory and infinite-dimensional topology
fields.description: Compact connected spaces, Peano continua and space-filling curves, absolute retracts, hyperspaces, the Hilbert cube and fixed-point properties.

fields.title: Topological groups
fields.description: Groups carrying a compatible topology: metrizability, profinite groups and profinite completions, and functions on locally compact groups.

fields.title: Algebraic topology
fields.description: Homotopy groups, singular homology and other algebraic invariants of spaces, with classical theorems such as Borsuk–Ulam, Hurewicz and Hopf invariant one.

fields.title: Manifolds and geometric topology
fields.description: Topological and smooth manifolds in low and high dimensions: surfaces, 3- and 4-manifolds, the Poincaré conjecture, exotic spheres, triangulations, diffeomorphism groups and transformation groups.

fields.title: Knot theory
fields.description: Embeddings of circles in three-space up to ambient isotopy: knot and link diagrams, chirality, slice knots, and geometric invariants such as ropelength, distortion and quadrisecants.
